Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Duncan Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Pitt hasn't allowed a point in the first or third quarter this season. Pitt also hasn't left Pittsburgh. That changes today at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, when the Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) walk into a sold-out Lane Stadium to face a Virginia Tech team (4-0, 1-0 ACC) chasing its first 5-0 start since 2005. The winner moves into a three-way tie for first place in the ACC. "It'll be one of the louder games we play," Pitt head coach Pat Narduzzi said this week. Here are three bold predictions for the game. 1. Jeffrey Overton Jr. runs for 100 yards on the nation's No. 4 run defense Pitt has allowed 213 rushing yards in four games. Overton ran for 209 yards last Saturday at Boston College, including the 76-yard touchdown that put Virginia Tech ahead for good in a 21-14 win. That earned him ACC Running Back of the Week. The sophomore missed the first eight games of last season with an injury and finished 2025 with 25 carries. He already has 60 this fall, for 409 yards and four rushing touchdowns at 6.8 yards per carry. He'll run Friday without left tackle Justin Terry, who is out. That's a real problem against a defense allowing 53.3 rushing yards per game. 2. Mason Heintschel leaves Blacksburg without a touchdown pass Pitt's sophomore quarterback has thrown 13 touchdown passes, second in the ACC. Seven came against Miami (Ohio). Six came against Bucknell. Against UCF and Syracuse, he went 28 of 52 for 335 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. The Panthers got past Syracuse by running for 245 yards, and true freshman running back Damon Ferguson Jr. leads the team with 239 yards for the season. Virginia Tech has to take that away first. Then comes the hard part for Heintschel. This is his first road start of the season, against a defense that leads the nation with 45 tackles for loss and 17 sacks. The risk sits behind Virginia Tech's front. Maryland threw for 359 yards and three touchdowns on the Hokies two weeks ago, and Virginia Tech has one interception in four games. Defensive coordinator Brent Pry's group doesn't have to be perfect. It has to make Heintschel uncomfortable, and no defense in the country has lived in the backfield more. 3. John Love hits a walk-off field goal, and Virginia Tech is ranked by Sunday John Love has scored 313 points in a Virginia Tech uniform. The next three decide Friday night. "This is going to be a battle," Virginia Tech head coach James Franklin said Monday. Franklin would know. He faced Narduzzi four times from 2016-19 when he was at Penn State. Pitt leads the ACC at 8.5 points allowed per game and hasn't given up more than 14 to anyone. I have Virginia Tech get past that number, but not by much. The Panthers stay in it on the ground, the way they did against Syracuse. That leaves it to Love. The fifth-year kicker is fourth on Virginia Tech's all-time scoring list, has a career-long of 60 yards, and went 2 for 2 at Boston College. He gets one more with the clock running out. Virginia Tech wins 24-21. The Hokies have 86 points in the AP poll, fifth among teams outside the Top 25, and haven't been ranked since 2021.With a win on Friday night, it will be hard to leave them out for another week. picks.headline: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt
picks.blurb: Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Division series preview Valkyries take down Wings 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Full Game Preview and Score Prediction for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Virginia Tech Athletics Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium - this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel has completed 88 of 130 passes for 1,191 yards, 13 touchdowns and just one interception. His season began with a historic seven-touchdown performance against Miami (Ohio), and he threw for 403 yards and six touchdowns in last week's demolition of Bucknell. Heintschel became the first ACC quarterback to record multiple six-touchdown passing games in the same season. That should provide Virginia Tech's pass rush with its biggest challenge yet. The Hokies have consistently disrupted opposing backfields, entering Friday averaging 4.25 sacks and 11.3 tackles for loss per game. Cortez Harris has led that charge with five sacks, including two in the victory over Boston College. Getting to Heintschel could be critical. Pitt averages 347.3 passing yards and 39.3 points per game, and its passing attack isn't dependent on a single target. Thirteen different Panthers caught a pass against Bucknell, while five players hauled in touchdowns. Censere Lee led the scoring barrage with three touchdown receptions. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. Pitt is 3-8 all-time in Blacksburg, although the Panthers have won three of the last four overall meetings between the programs. Virginia Tech won the most recent matchup, 38-21, in 2023. Virginia Tech has answered four different tests through four weeks. Pitt presents another, and perhaps the most complete one yet. One undefeated record will disappear Friday night. Which one do I think will? Virginia Tech's defense should give Pitt its toughest test yet, while Lane Stadium could make the Panthers' first road game uncomfortable. The Hokies may not completely contain Heintschel, but Overton and Grunkemeyer should generate enough offense late to preserve the unbeaten start in a tightly contested ACC matchup. Virginia Tech Athleticse Thomas Hughes Fri, October 2, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads BLACKSBURG, Va. - Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I'm predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech's defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin's team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Pittsburgh Panthers: News, Updates, and Predictions
picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. Pittsburgh Panthers: News, Updates, and Predictions | Gobbler Country Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Virginia Tech Hokies Community Gobbler Country October 3, 2026 Gobbler Country Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech Basketball Virginia Tech Baseball Betting FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Virginia Tech Football Odds Virginia Tech Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Virginia Tech Football Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Virginia Tech Football Virginia Tech hosts the Pittsburgh Panthers in an old fashioned Big East grudge match. Tech is a narrow homefield favorite, but the media and commentariat don’t agree. It’s looking like a season where the upcoming game is the most important game of the season. If you had to pick a really obvious one out of the stack, the Pitt game runs right to the top of the flagpole. Let’s look at some team news, a few updates here and there, and then get to the predictions. It’s not Homecoming, but It is Stripe Lane Night The program has fan gimmicks for most games this season, and it’s a night where certain sections wear orange, and others wear maroon. Sometimes it works out, and sometimes it sort of looks like more than half the people didn’t care or didn’t know. Just a Reminder that the Team in Maroon Earned Its Way Last Saturday in a New England coastal Nor’easter, the Hokies earned their respect the hard way, by fighting BC and the weather to catch, pass, and then burn out the clock before they had a chance to respond. Jeffrey Overton, Jr. Gets Some Kudos He gets named ACC Running Back of the Week for his powerful performance in the rain and wind of Alumni Stadium. PFF picks out Overton but also adds Quentin Reddish and Jaquez White for their National Team of the Week notice. Catch Up with Coach Franklin’s Weekly Presser This is nearly a 51-minute watch so go grab a coffee. Lots of good information in this one. Predictions Time Huge game for the Hokies. This game means a lot for several reasons. A chance to go 5-0, a chance to go 2-0 in the ACC, a chance to re-establish Lane Stadium as a place that visiting teams dread coming to play. Pitt is a tough challenge. Under Pat Narduzzi, the Panthers always play a tough brand of football. They generally play solid defense and rely on the running game. They now have a quarterback who can air it out. Pitt’s strengths and Virginia Tech’s potential weaknesses match up well for the Panthers. The Hokies have allowed some big plays through the air this year, so Pitt will test that. I have concerns about Pitt’s run defense. The Hokies have had some issues at times this year and are dealing with multiple injuries along the offensive line. That’s something to watch. I do think the Hokies will make some plays in the running game. More Jeffrey Overton, please. Luke Reynolds had a down game last week, due to the weather more than anything, but I expect a big bounce-back this week. Reynolds catches another touchdown and quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer is the better quarterback on the field again this week. It’s close, but the Hokies win. Virginia Tech 27, Pitt 21 Tough games require some tough thinking. This one is essentially a toss-up, and regardless of these two teams’ records they always seem to be a fist fight street brawl. This season neither team is ranked, but neither is showing up at Lane Stadium with a loss on their record. Tech is rallying up behind a completely revamped and very different offense than we have seen since the Michael Brewer days at the end of the Beamer Era. This Tech team has an actual quarterback, uses its tight ends and gets downfield with intermediate distance pass plays. The defensive style isn’t much different than has been fielded in the past, but the line is bigger and a bit faster than we are used to. It still has problems with running quarterbacks, and the secondary has just not stiffened yet. That’s a concern for this one because Nardo has found a good quarterback, too, and as we saw in the recent past when he has a good quarterback his teams go from wobbly to competitive. To win this Tech has to drive and score on nearly every possession. The defense needs to get fast “A” gap pressure on Pitt’s QB, and the secondary needs to stiffen up considerably. It’s also going to need to avoid any “prevent” situations since Pitt can score fast if it needs to. Add all that stuff up, and this one is going to be one of two things. A runaway with one team dominating over the other with fast offensive and heavy defensive pressure, or both teams are going to force a tough close contest. I am thinking the latter is more likely, I still have pictures in the library of the 4th quarter 4th and Goal for Pitt at the Tech 2. This stacks up to be, in my mind anyway, a similar contest. I think Tech takes it, but it’s going to be close, a 3- or 4-point difference. Both teams are probably good for scores in the mid- to high- twenties. The team that breaks 30 wins. 31 - 24 Hokies Just a Reminder About Friday Evening If you are coming to the game, check your seat against the chart, and wear the appropriate color. We’ll be on the field, cameras going, stay with us for pictures on the Facebook page Saturday evening. GO HOKIES!!!! picks.blurb: Penn State vs. Northwestern Predictions: Week 5 Stress Test for Nittany Lions Skip to main content SI.COM OLYMPIC SPORTS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS A year ago, James Franklin walked off the Beaver Stadium field for the last time after Penn State's 22-21 loss to Northwestern. The Wildcats turned a fourth-quarter drive into the game-winning touchdown that ended Franklin's tenure as Penn State's head coach. On Friday night, the Nittany Lions get another crack at the Wildcats, this time as part of a grand opening. Northwestern will host Penn State in the first game at the new Ryan Field, a nearly $900 million venue that claims to be the most expensive college stadium ever built. There are plenty of Penn State storylines Friday night beyond a mostly new program getting proxy retribution for last year's loss at Beaver Stadium. More than half of Penn State's roster wasn't on the field that night and doesn't care about settling scores. These Nittany Lions want to settle their offense. With that in mind, here's how we see Friday's Penn State-Northwestern game shaking out, including our predictions from the Penn State on SI staff. Kickoff is scheduled for just after 8 p..m. ET on FOX. 1. Meanwhile, there's a big football game between Penn State (3-1) and Northwestern (2-1) teams that each lost their Big Ten openers, but in very different ways. The Wildcats held up well in an entertaining 29-23 fight at Indiana, and the Nittany Lions collapsed late in a 24-20 thriller against Wisconsin . Now, these two get a lovely place to play their important Friday night conference game. Penn State vs Northwestern: Quick Hits Penn State gets USC after this, followed up by a date at Michigan . Northwestern gets another home game against Ball State next, and then goes to Michigan State for a showdown against former head coach Pat Fitzgerald. A loss would make it the second year in a row that Penn State started 0-2 in the Big Ten and 3-2 overall. The Nittany Lions lead the nation in third down stops, allowing teams to convert just 19.2% of their chances. Northwestern is okay offensively on third downs, but the defense allowed Indiana to convert 60% of their tries. Northwestern doesn't live off forcing mistakes, but it needs them in this. However, Penn State turned it over just once and has only been flagged 19 times in four games. Why Northwestern Will Win Aidan Chiles has been wonderful. The transfer quarterback from Michigan State was amazing over the last two games against Colorado and Indiana, completing over 75% of his passes with five touchdowns and no picks. He might not be running like he normally does, but his slippery style should be a problem for a Penn State defense that's not doing much to get into the backfield so far. The Nittany Lions have only come up with six sacks so far. Penn State vs Northwestern Prediction, Betting Lines Penn State's offense was terrific over the first three games, but that was against Marshall, Temple , and Buffalo. It'll come out sharp with the midrange passing game, but the running game that's been missing against everyone but Temple won't get the invite to the party. The Nittany Lion defense will hold up well in a tough fight, the offense will pull off a big late scoring drive, and … Northwestern will walk it off with Jackson Kleather – he has yet to miss a kick – hitting the game-winner. picks.headline: Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State
picks.blurb: Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus Division series preview Valkyries take down Wings 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Week 5 Game Predictions: Northwestern Wildcats vs. Penn State Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Northwestern will return home Friday night when the Wildcats take on Penn State in the highly anticipated first game at New Ryan Field . Northwestern enters the matchup with a 2-1 record after falling just short in a 29-23 loss to No. 5 Indiana , while Penn State comes to Evanston at 3-1 after suffering a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Wildcats will look to bounce back from their first loss of the season while beginning a new era in front of a large crowd. Penn State will also be looking to get back in the win column after allowing a 17-0 lead to slip away against the Badgers. The game is scheduled for 7 p.m. CT Friday at New Ryan Field and will air nationally on FOX. Here are our predictions for Friday's historic matchup. Alex Kwiatkowski (3-0): Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 I'm taking Northwestern to open the new Ryan Field era with a win. The Wildcats are starting to look like a team that can truly compete in the Big Ten. Northwestern entered last week as a 23.5-point underdog against No. 5 Indiana but nearly pulled off the upset, eventually falling 29-23 in Bloomington. What impressed me most was how Northwestern responded after a terrible first half. The Wildcats trailed 12-0 at halftime but refused to go away, scoring 23 points in the second half and putting themselves in position to potentially win the game late. Aidan Chiles continues to look comfortable in Chip Kelly's offense, and Northwestern has shown it has multiple weapons in the passing game. Chiles threw for 293 yards and accounted for three touchdowns against Indiana, while Luke Dehnicke and Griffin Wilde combined for 196 receiving yards. Sep 25, 2026; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Northwestern Wildcats quarterback Aidan Chiles (0) scores a touchdown against Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Kaiden Turner (14) during the second half at Merchants Bank Field at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images Now, Northwestern gets to return home with plenty of excitement surrounding the program. Friday will mark the first game at New Ryan Field, and the stadium is sold out. I expect the Wildcats to feed off the energy and come out hot in front of what should be one of the best home atmospheres Northwestern has experienced in years. Penn State, meanwhile, enters at a low point after blowing a 17-0 lead in a 24-20 loss to Wisconsin. The Nittany Lions will be motivated to bounce back, but I think Northwestern carries its momentum from the second half against Indiana into Friday night. I expect Chiles and the offense to put points on the board early, while the defense does enough to keep Penn State from finding a consistent rhythm. Northwestern begins its new era with a statement win. Prediction: Northwestern 30, Penn State 24 Nick Meyer (2-0): Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 The Wildcats looked like a Big Ten title contender on the road against Indiana last week, while Penn State was upset at home by Wisconsin. I expect Northwestern to be fired up for the opening game at New Ryan Field, but I also expect the Wildcats to make a few mistakes due to the emotions and jitters surrounding such a historic night. This should be another close game, but Northwestern is expected to be without tight end Luke Dehnicke, who had a huge performance against Indiana with seven receptions for 140 yards. His absence would take away one of Aidan Chiles' most productive targets. This is a winnable game for Northwestern, but I expect Penn State to have the advantage in the trenches on both sides of the ball. Ultimately, that will be enough for the Nittany Lions to escape Evanston with a close win. Prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24

picks.blurb: Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB March Madness Get Fantasy Plus Division series preview Valkyries take down Wings 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Penn State Given Interesting Prediction Ahead of Northwestern Matchup (Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images) Matt Levine Thu, October 1, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Penn State Nittany Lions will be looking to get back on track tomorrow against Northwestern , in what could be a tough game for the team. Penn State fell 24-20 to Wisconsin last week in what was one of the more surprising scores from the weekend. But the Nittany Lions believe that the loss to the Badgers was more of an outlier, and this team still has a lot to play for this year. As the team gets ready for the Wildcats, the Nittany Lions will need to make sure that they don't overlook them. Northwestern has played much better to start the season than they have in year's past, opening the year 2-1 under head coach David Braun. For Penn State, this can be a bounce-back game, with the team getting things right after the tough loss against Wisconsin. But Friday night games can be tough, especially having to go on the road. Heading into the game, the Nittany Lions are favored to win the contest, but not by too much. According to ESPN , Penn State is being given a 55.9 percent chance to take down Northwestern on the road. If the Nittany Lions are going to win this game, everything starts and end with quarterback Rocco Becht . Becht has looked good to open the year, throwing for 865 yards with nine touchdowns and one interception. But against the Badgers, Becht struggled, throwing for just 114 yards and one interception. The veteran signal-caller will need to get back on track in this game against Northwestern if the Nittany Lions are to have a shot at winning. Coming over from Iowa State with head coach Matt Campbell, Becht gives Penn State a legitimate option under center. But he has bene prone to some inconsistency at times during his career, and last week was one of those moments for him. Northwestern has its own star quarterback in Aidan Chiles , who transferred to the team this offseason. So far, Chiles has played very well for the Wildcats, throwing for 807 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions. If Penn State can find a way to slow him down, it could make life much easier to grab the win. But Chiles has turned this offense around, and this will be something that the Nittany Lions will need to focus on throughout the game. Overall, Penn State needs to take down Northwestern if they want a chance to make the College Football Playoff this year. The Nittany Lions are off to a good a start this year, even with the loss last week, and this game offers them a chance to turn the page.

The Nittany Lions will visit Northwestern on Friday evening as the Wildcats proudly open the doors to the newly renovated Ryan Field for the first time. That figures to make for a bit of a challenge as Northwestern will be fired up to show off their new digs and pick up a big win in conference play after an incredible effort last week on the road against Indiana. On the other hand, Penn State is merely looking to rebound after a tough loss at home last week to Wisconsin that saw the Nittany Lions blow a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. The optimism for Penn State on the road against Northwestern may have dipped in the span of the past week, for good and understandable reasons, but the staff at Nittany Lions Wire still seems to think Penn State will find a way to come out of the week with a win. Here are our final score and player of the game predictions for Penn State's Week 5 game against Northwestern, along with some brief thoughts on the matchup. Kevin McGuire, Lead Writer We saw last week that Penn State's offense really missed the likes of rising star wide receiver Koby Howard. This week, there can be no excuse for not having something going in the passing game. I think that means Rocco Becht needs to get into a comfort zone with his tight ends a bit more instead of looking for some big plays down the field from the receivers. So for the second week in a row, I'm looking for Ben BRahmer to be a difference maker for the offense. If Penn State can get that, then they should be in good enough shape to get out of Evanston with a hard-fought win. Northwestern will not make anything easy on the Nittany Lions. This may need to be a bit of a scrappy win from the offense. Final score prediction: Penn State 20, Northwestern 18 Player of the game pick: Ben Brahmer, Penn State tight end Paul White, Contributor This Northwestern team just took Indiana down to the wire, so I'd imagine a Penn State win would have to be in a close game. That doesn't sound like such a fun idea after last week's game, but hopefully we can keep our composure this time Final score prediction: Penn State 27, Northwestern 24 Player of the game pick: Chase Sowell, Penn State wide receiver Christopher Sheppard, Contributor The Nittany Lions find themselves in a similar position to last year as they face Northwestern after an inexplicable loss yet again. This time, it's on the road as Northwestern opens up the new Ryan Field. In order to spoil affairs, the Nittany Lions have to get going in the passing game and take advantage of what could be an aggressive Wildcat defense. Look for Chase Sowell to step up in the continued absence of Koby Howard and be the difference in a game that could come down to the last few plays. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . away.headline: Penn State week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up
away.blurb: It’s still early in the year, but the injury bug has already bitten Penn State hard, forcing star wide receiver Koby Howard to miss the start of conference play. Howard’s absence was significant in the Nittany Lions Week 4 loss to Wisconsin, and he’ll be out again on Friday night when Matt Campbell’s team helps open the newly rebuilt Ryan Field at Northwestern. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. Dixson was on the initial injury report on Tuesday night, listed as “questionable,” and held the same status on Thursday night when the availability report was released about 24 hours before kickoff in Evanston. The return of Alex Tatsch, who missed Week 1 as he ramped up from an injury he suffered preparing for the Pinstripe Bowl in December, has helped to fill the void left by Smith and Kooper Ebel, and Tony Rojas has been rock-solid at the second level of D’Anton Lynn’s defense. Dixson is seemingly the only player on Penn State’s roster whose status is uncertain heading into Friday night. Considering he played through the injury in the second half against Wisconsin, his outlook appears favorable, but that he wasn’t upgraded to “probable” raises a legitimate question about whether or not he’ll be ready to suit up against the Wildcats. Notable Northwestern injuries: Luke Dehnicke still doubtful While not ruled out, Northwestern has two starters listed as doubtful for Friday night, including its second-leading receiver: tight end Luke Dehnicke. Dehnicke caught seven passes for 140 yards against Indiana in Week 4, but was banged up and could miss Week 5. The Wildcats may also be without starting defensive back Braden Turner. Fellow starting DB Damon Walters is listed as questionable. Here’s a look at the full report: This article was originally published on victorybellrings.com as Penn State Week 5 injury report vs. Northwestern: Who’s in, who’s out, and who has to step up . Howard, however, isn’t the only injury situation the Nittany Lions are dealing with. There’s another member of the 2025 recruiting class who has turned into a key cog for Penn State, whose situation is worth monitoring: cornerback Daryus Dixson. Penn State needs to get back into the win column after melting down in the second half last week, and Campbell is still in search of his first Big Ten win. To get it, the Nittany Lions will need to be at full strength. Here’s a look at the injury report: Cam Smith is the notable downgrade from the early-week report. The redshirt freshman linebacker hasn’t played a defensive snap for the Nittany Lions since Week 1, and though he’s lower on a crowded linebacker depth chart, he’s a promising young player whom Campbell spoke highly of in the preseason. If Dixson is unable to go, two other young defensive backs will likely have their numbers

picks.headline: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know
picks.blurb: Mississippi State vs. Alabama Prediction, TV Channel, Kickoff Time, Everything Fans Need to Know Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THINGS STATE SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS STARKVILLE — It's been nearly two decades since Mississippi State felt the joy of a win against Alabama. Sylvester Croom was roaming the sidelines as first-year coach Nick Saban and his Crimson Tide program were in the midst of a late season slide. Fast-forward 20 years and its Kalen DeBoer leading the way, looking to lead his team to 5-0 record for the first time in his tenure. On the flip side, Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby is looking to earn the first signature win of his young head coaching career while hosting No. 7 ranked Alabama for a nationally televised showdown on ABC. Here's everything you need to know to be prepared for what's a pivotal weekend for the Bulldogs program. Mississippi State Bulldogs running back Fluff Bothwell (24) and wide receiver Zion Ragins (7) react after a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Game Information Game Information Mississippi State vs. Alabama Crimson Tide When : Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 Kickoff Time : 11 a.m. CT Venue : Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville, Mississippi TV Channel : ABC Radio : Bulldogs Sports Network Series Record : Alabama leads 86-18-3 Betting : Alabama (-5.5), O/u: 60.5 total points ( FanDuel ) DISCLAIMER : Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. What ESPN Thinks The brand of Alabama remains strong on the national radar and that's no different this week at ESPN with the Crimson Tide given a 74.2% chance of going into one of the most hostile atmospheres in all of college football and pulling out a win, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Mississippi State State continues its climb up the FPI rating system, coming in this week at No. 9 among SEC teams and No. 20 overall with key victories on the road at Minnesota and South Carolina plus another against then No. 19 Missouri. This starts one of the stiffest stretches for any team as the Bulldogs are set for a murderer's row-level slate with Alabama coming Saturday, proceeded by a BYE, on the road at LSU, home against Oklahoma and then another road trip to Austin to face the Texas Longhorns. The Bulldogs chances of winning out are slim at 0.1%, but do have a 97.5% chance of at least reaching bowl eligibility with six wins. When it comes to making the playoffs, Lebby's team has the sixth-best odds SEC teams at 23.8% to at least make the field, 1.6% to make the championship game and 0.5% chance to win the national championship. ESPN FPI (SEC) Rankings 1. Georgia 2. Texas 3. Alabama 4. LSU 5. Florida 6. Tennessee 7. Texas A&M 8. Ole Miss 9. Mississippi State 10. Oklahoma 11. Auburn 12. South Carolina 13. Missouri 14. Kentucky 15. Vanderbilt 16. Arkansas Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Kalen DeBoer walks off the field after a victory against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What DeBoer Is Saying What DeBoer Is Saying One of the hardest things for a coach to prepare his team for in a road game at Davis-Wade Stadium is the cadence of cowbells. Thousands of cowbells. "Personally, this is one of those stadiums that I haven't played in no matter where I've been," DeBoer said Monday. "What I hear from the people that I trust, is that it's going to be an absolutely crazy environment. We're going to be prepared for that. We talked about as a team this morning and we're looking forward to that challenge. "We know, this week, we've got to work on that crowd noise. There will probably be a lot of cowbells that we're hearing in practice in one form or fashion. Another thing is that it's just an early game. It's an 11 o'clock kickoff. We're a morning practice team and we've had some success in those morning games. We've got to go on the road and travel that morning. It's going to be a little different set-up that way too." The Bulldogs' defense has been very active this season at stopping explosive plays and keeping everything in front of them. They're disciplined, bring elite energy and effort with each down. "They play complementary football. They get the ball back, get off the field and get the ball back to the offense. I think it's timely stops. It's a group effort of guys flying around. They're going to be multiple in what they show you. "I have a lot of respect for them and what they are doing this time of the year. I think complementary football is what they're doing really well at Mississippi State. They're explosive. Obviously, that defense has to face that offense every day in practice. It's high level across the board." Mississippi State Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby looks on during the second quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Lebby Is Saying What Lebby Is Saying The Crimson Tide offense is full of big play athletes at nearly every position. Whether that's done with Keelon Russell's dual-threat combination, a four-headed backfield, Ryan Williams or any other weapon, Lebby knows his defense has to play assignment-driven, technically sound football to avoid allowing the game to get away from them early. "We're gonna have to do a great job tackling," Lebby said. "That's gonna be a huge piece of it. He's played really well. He's been incredibly productive. There's been explosive plays. He's got great talent around him. And so for us it's going to be about applying pressure, getting our fans really involved and excited about what's going on in between those white lines. "So for us it's kinda like I mentioned. We gotta get him off the spot and we've got to do a great job taking air out of it on the back end and making the plays when we get the chance." Alabama is tied for No. 24 nationally in sacks with 11 on the season. On the otherhand, Mississippi State has given up nine sacks on the season, which ranks No. 9 nationally, but the most alarming number was the four given up against Missouri in last week's 31-24 victory. And Lebby knows the biggest key to the Bulldogs upset bid will be keeping star quarterback Kamario Taylor upright to further establish himself as a Heisman Trophy contender. “[We] had moments where we were really clean, and had moments where we’ve got to continue to clean up,” Lebby said. “The fundamental pieces of it I’m gonna continue to talk about. Those guys playing clean fundamentally gives us the best chance to protect 1, but there were issues from a game standpoint. "We didn’t do a great job on the penetrator a couple times, and that’s part of being able to clean that up as we watch the tape, a huge focus for us this week.” Prediction : Mississippi State 42, Alabama 38 Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Former UCLA Coach Rick Neuheisel Predicts Winner of Alabama-Mississippi State Game Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0) travels to Davis Wade Stadium to face No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0) in the SEC's lone ranked matchup of Week 5 (Noon EDT, ABC). These two programs are separated by an hour and a half's driving distance and are meeting for the first time in three seasons. Alabama and Mississippi State have been traditional staples on each other's schedules, although the 86-18-3 advantage held by the Crimson Tide makes for the most lopsided series in SEC history. The Bulldogs' last victory was in 2007, Nick Saban's first season in Tuscaloosa. The closest Mississippi State came within the last 16 meetings was in 2017; the game was tied in the final 30 seconds, and Jalen Hurts hit then-freshman wide receiver DeVonta Smith for a 26-yard touchdown pass to win it 31-24. The matchup features a pair of high-octane offenses Sep 26, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) throws the ball during the first quarter against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Alabama has scored 45 points or more in each of its first four games. The Crimson Tide did run back interceptions for touchdowns in three of those four, but that means the offense has scored no fewer than 38 points in a game to start the season. Keelon Russell has been fantastic for Alabama, but the most impressive part of the offense is the run game. The Crimson Tide has been questionable in that department for the better part of three seasons, and it has very quickly found a combination of offensive linemen and running backs to correct the deficiency. On the other side, Kamario Taylor has lived up to the hype for Mississippi State. He guided the Bulldogs to a pair of road wins at Minnesota and South Carolina to bring excitement to a fan base desperate for optimism, and he delivered a 31-24 win over Missouri to a packed Davis Wade Stadium under the lights in Week 4. Neuheisel: "I see two matchups here that are really cool." CBS Sports' "Inside College Football" panel predicted the winner of the game between Alabama and Mississippi State on Tuesday. Former UCLA head coach Rick Neuheisel pointed to a pair of critical matchups between the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs while making his game pick. "Number one is the quarterbacks," Neuheisel said . "These two guys are both going to play on Sundays, both have just unique frames. They're 19 years old and they're just getting started." Despite the intrigue in the quarterback matchup, Neuheisel pointed to the other matchup as a deciding factor due to the current weather forecast for Saturday. "The second matchup is between the two defensive coordinators," Neuheisel said. "Both have been head coaches: Kane Wommack was at South Alabama, Zach Arnett was ironically right here at Mississippi State, these guys know how to play field position defense. It's supposed to rain a lot during the game, I think I've got to go, in that situation with Alabama." Loading recommendations... picks.blurb: Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Division series preview Valkyries take down Wings 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Alabama Receives Nerve-Wracking Prediction vs Mississippi State (David Leong-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Thu, October 1, 2026 at 1:32 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Alabama Crimson Tide are coming off of a dominant Week 4 win over South Carolina, which represented their most complete performance all season. Now, Alabama is preparing for its most difficult test yet , as the Crimson Tide are heading on the road to battle the upstart Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday. Like Alabama, Mississippi State is 4-0, and the Bulldogs are also fresh off of a very impressive victory, having topped Missouri last weekend. Mississippi State boasts an explosive offense, and while its defense certainly isn't among the best, it has a pair of terrific cornerbacks in Kelley Jones and Jett Jefferson that could pose some problems for Keelon Russell and Co. So, are the Crimson Tide on upset alert heading into Week 5? ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score of the matchup using his SP+ metrics, and while he does have Alabama coming out on top, he thinks it will be a nail-biter, projecting a 32-27 win for the Tide in Starkville. A victory would absolutely comprise Alabama's most impressive of the campaign to date and would set Kalen DeBoer's squad up very nicely as it continues to proceed into the most challenging part of its schedule, which begins with the clash against the Bulldogs. While the Crimson Tide are undefeated, things haven't necessarily been easy for them thus far. Alabama took care of business without breaking a sweat against East Carolina in its season opener, but it trailed Kentucky 17-13 at halftime in Week 2 before dominating the second half. It also fell behind Florida State 21-6 in the first half the following week, but ultimately rallied for a 50-36 victory. The Crimson Tide definitely avoided a slow start versus South Carolina last Saturday, taking a 35-3 lead at one point in a 49-18 triumph. One thing is for sure: the version of Alabama that showed up in Weeks 2 and 3 absolutely cannot expect to waltz into Mississippi State and emerge with a victory. The Bulldogs are a significantly better team than either Kentucky or South Carolina, and the Crimson Tide fall behind early, they could be in some serious trouble. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the top Heisman Trophy candidates at the moment, and the Bulldogs also possess a terrific backfield led by Fluff Bothwell. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has also been a fast riser, too. Alabama cannot mess around this weekend.

away.headline: Trump says he will attend Georgia-Alabama football game in Tuscaloosa
away.blurb: President Trump announced Friday that he will be returning to Alabama next week for the University of Georgia vs. University of Alabama college football game. He made the announcement while in Mobile, Ala. for a rally as part of his travels to several different states to rally Republicans ahead of the midterms. The game is set to take place on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 7:30 p.m. EDT at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa. The Georgia Bulldogs and Alabama Crimson Tide are currently ranked second and seventh, respectively, in this week's AP Top 25 . Trump attended the University of Texas vs. University of Tennessee college football game in Knoxville last week. It was the first game he attended since January’s College Football Playoff National Championship when Indiana University defeated the University of Miami. Trump has attended several sports events throughout his second term, including the FIFA World Cup finals in July and the Super Bowl in 2025. Earlier this month he attended the Irish Open at the Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg, Ireland. He also hosted a UFC fight on the South Lawn of the White House in June. away.headline: Will Jayvin James play for Alabama vs. Miss. State? Final injury update for Tide's RT
away.blurb: Alabama starting RT Jayvin James went down in the fourth quarter of the Crimson Tide's 49-18 win over South Carolina last week. Kalen DeBoer called him questionable on Monday, and he carried that injury designation through Wednesday and Thursday's availability reports. But on Friday night, James was officially ruled out. Jayvin James ruled out, JUCO transfer Tyrell Miller will start for Alabama at Mississippi State Will Jayvin James play for Alabama vs. Miss. State? Final injury update for Tide's RT Skip to main content About BH Alabama Football Alabama Football Alabama Football All-Time Lists Alabama Basketball Alabama Basketball Alabama Basketball All-Time Lists It's a difficult blow for the Crimson Tide ahead of a game in which the offense will need to be at its best with Mississippi State's ability to score points. It's also a difficult blow for James, as this was a game he undoubtedly had circled on his calendar. He transferred to Alabama after playing for Mississippi State last season. Alabama will now turn to JUCO transfer Tyrell Miller, who will make his first start for the Crimson Tide. Miller started the season listed as Alabama's backup left tackle behind sophomore Jackson Lloyd. But at some point, he and Texas transfer Nick Brooks swapped sides of the offensive line, and Miller has been the backup at RT. He got into the game last week against South Carolina, playing 14 total snaps. Miller held up well in relief, flashing his athleticism and ability to execute in this system at a high level. If you have any concerns about his ability to step in for James, I would encourage you to watch Landon Tengwall's film breakdown of Miller's snaps against the Gamecocks: Miller is a guy the coaching staff has been high on throughout the offseason. He has worked as Alabama's sixth offensive lineman through the first four weeks in heavier packages. He was one of the more underrated portal pickups for Kalen DeBoer and company this offseason. Miller spent the first two years of his career at San Mateo Junior College in California. He was expected to serve in a reserve role this season and potentially compete for a starting job heading into 2027. But the injury to James will thrust him into the lineup sooner than expected. The good news is that Miller appears to be ahead of schedule from what the expectations were when he arrived in Tuscaloosa. Alabama has already navigated one SEC road game without a starter up front. Alabama traveled to Kentucky in Week 2 and beat the Wildcats without starting RG Michael Carroll . In Week 5 against Mississippi State, they'll have to find a way to win without James. picks.blurb: 3 Predictions for Michigan Football Against Minnesota Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Michigan Wolverines will take on the Minnesota Golden Gophers on Saturday in their first road game of the season. The Wolverines are reeling coming off a 20-19 loss at home to the Iowa Hawkeyes, and need to bounce back before the schedule at the end of the season gets daunting. This is not your father’s Minnesota team. They are tough, resilient, and playing good football after last week’s 27-24 win over the Washington Huskies. PJ Fleck may be a little odd, but he has his team playing well. Will that be enough to spring an upset over the Wolverines who are favored on the road? Here are some of our predictions for Michigan’s first road game of the season. Jordan Marshall Goes for 100 Yards Jordan Marshall says he’s good to go. We’re taking him at his word here, but the Michigan run game needs to find some traction. The Wolverines have been putrid on the ground this season, and rank 92nd in the nation in yards-per-game . Michigan’s task did not get any easier this week, as Minnesota’s run defense has been stingy to start the year. This is the type of defense where run plays need to have yards come after the running back is first contacted. When he is healthy, that is Jordan Marshall’s specialty. He gives the Wolverines a personality in their run game, and is a violent runner. Last week, it looked like he was getting on track and running as hard as he has all season before curiously being out of the game for the final possession. Marshall is going to be the man, he’ll have some short runs earlier that turn into long runs as Michigan plays into the body-blow theory. The bet here also is that Marshall breaks a run for an explosive gain, which the Wolverines have not had on the ground for one of their running backs this season. Marshall tops the century mark for the first time for any Wolverine rusher this season. Michigan Defense Gets 3 Takeaways Where are the takeaways? Michigan’s defense has been great in almost every metric this season, but have been unable to take the ball away enough. The Wolverines had two takeaways against Oklahoma, and one against UTEP. That’s it so far this season, and their offense has been too sloppy with the ball. The result is that Michigan is currently minus-3 in the turnover margin. Yes, Michigan needs to play cleaner on offense, but their defense needs to start making some plays as well. That’s a compliment, but also means he might put the ball in harm’s way. The bet this week is Michigan picks off two passes and gets a strip sack from someone we’re predicting as the star of the game. Tariq Boney is the Star of the Show Whether John Henry Daley plays or not, he’s likely to play on a reduced snap count thanks to a leg injury he suffered on the second-to-last play of last week’s game against Iowa. That will mean more snaps for the backup defensive ends. Tariq Boney has been productive whenever he has been on the field. He often reminds me of Chase Winovich during the 2016 season. Winovich did not play much on run downs, but was tasked with getting after the quarterback in obvious passing situations. That could be Boney’s role throughout the season, even if it’s not a perfect comparison between the two players. After losing four straight Little Brown Jug games under PJ Fleck, Minnesota looks to end its losing streak against Michigan on Saturday at noon ET (FOX). The Wolverines are 5.5-point favorites, and my Michigan vs. Minnesota combos and college football picks are backing Kyle Whittingham's defense and Bryce Underwood's legs. Best Michigan vs Minnesota combos For help understanding probabilities, see our odds calculator . Michigan vs Minnesota combo Since 1968, the Michigan vs. Minnesota rivalry hasn't been much of a rivalry, with Minnesota going 44-4. Minnesota head coach PJ Fleck hasn't had any luck ending the Wolverines' dominance, either, losing all four games with the Little Brown Jug on the line. Under Fleck, the Golden Gophers haven't been very competitive, going 1-3 ATS and losing by an average margin of 40.2-17 — and my Michigan vs. Minnesota prediction expects Fleck to add another tick in the loss column. While the Wolverines just fell to Iowa on the final play, they outplayed the Hawkeyes and should have won by double digits. Even in the loss, the Wolverines allowed just 20 points, and seven of them came on a kick return touchdown. Michigan's defense is ranked No. 9 by SP+ and sits eighth in EPA per rush, 24th in EPA per pass, and 16th in available yards percentage (33.6%) . Considering Minnesota's inability to run the ball ( 103rd in EPA per rush ), the Wolverines can focus on stopping Drake Lindsey and win this one by 6+ points. Michigan vs Minnesota player prop combo If Michigan wants to retain the Little Brown Jug and cover the spread, it needs to stop Lindsey. Luckily, for the Wolverines faithful, Michigan has one of the best pass defenses in the country, led by veteran cornerbacks and a ferocious pass rush. The Wolverines' defense ranks 11th nationally in pass success rate (33.9%) , and its front seven has racked up 12 sacks and 71 pressures. That will make it difficult for Lindsey to throw for 215+ yards, something he's done just three times in his last 12 games. It will be hard for Michigan to get production through the air, too, but wide receiver JJ Buchanan is an X-factor. The Utah transfer has been the Wolverines' best player this season (he caught the Hail Mary against Western Michigan) and ranks top 12 nationally in receiving yards (396) and touchdowns (4) . Buchanan's size (6-foot-4) and ball skills (0 drops) should be a mismatch, especially near the end zone. But the biggest key to a Michigan win might be Bryce Underwood's mobility. In Jason Beck's system, the former five-star's legs have been utilized far more consistently. He's averaging 48 rushing yards per game and sits 10th among QBs in forced missed tackles (14). Minnesota's run defense has been underwhelming this season, ranking 107th in rush success rate (48.2%), so expect Underwood to be a large part of Michigan's run game. Michigan vs Minnesota Odds Michigan vs Minnesota point spread : Michigan -5.5 (-112), Minnesota +5.5 (-108) Michigan vs Minnesota over/under : 43.5 (-108o / -112u) Michigan vs Minnesota moneyline : Michigan -220, Minnesota +175 I am so unimpressed with Michigan . Not to beat a dead horse, but this team should be 2-2 after sneaking past Western Michigan in the first game, and then falling to Iowa in a buzzer-beater last week. In between those two games, the Wolverines also beat Oklahoma by the mere score of 17-10. The run game is probably the most unspectacular aspect of Michigan's game. Leading rusher Jordan Marshall is fine, but his 4.3 yards per carry is hardly moving mountains, and quarterback Bryce Underwood has only two fewer rushing yards than him. Speaking of Underwood, I've also expected better from a number-one overall recruit from his class – especially given the payday that he received to play in Ann Arbor. He has formed a great chemistry with JJ Buchanan, who leads the team in receiving on just under 20 yards per catch, along with Andrew Marsh, who leads in receptions. But that's where the problem lies. Buchanan and Marsh account for 71% of Michigan's receptions combined, and because of that, opponents know where Underwood is looking. It's either Buchanan, Marsh, or he'll take it for himself. On the defensive side of the ball is where the Wolverines thrive at a high level. Against the pass, they're ranked 13th in Success Rate allowed in pass plays, and ninth in Success Rate allowed in pass downs. Additionally, they do a high-end job at stuffing the run, ranking 13th in the FBS in opponent rushing yards allowed per game. PJ Fleck is a madman. I can't get the visual of him wiping a bloody nose off one of his players and draping it on his face out of my head. A true sicko. The Gophers are looking to secure their first home win over Michigan since 1977, and last week's win against Washington proved that they can do it. Michigan is vulnerable after losing to Iowa at the last second, and I think this is one of the rare times that Minnesota has the upper hand here. Minnesota likes to wear down its opponents, as showcased in Seattle last week. Its one loss was suffered against Mississippi State , one of the most dynamic teams in college football. Quarterback Drake Lindsey has been pretty efficient in his second season as the starter, completing passes at a 66% rate with seven touchdowns and two picks. And so far, he's revived the chemistry he formed with Javon Tracy last season, while seamlessly connecting with Cincinnati transfer Noah Jennings. In a complete 180, Minnesota doesn't like to run the ball a lot, ranking 134th in rushing attempts per game. A total shock, considering that Fleck likes to establish the run. TJ Thomas has been a total stud for the Gophers, rushing for 7.1 yards per carry and helping them achieve a 43rd Rush Play Success Rate. Defensively, this team does a fine job at holding down the fort. Fleck promoted Danny Collins as the defensive coordinator, and currently, the Gophers rank sixth overall in Havoc and 50th overall in points allowed. Did it seem like I was too harsh on Michigan? Because I thought I took it lightly on the maize and blue. I think this is a fascinating matchup because Michigan's defense has been stellar, but I wonder how the Wolverines fare on the offensive side. You also have to imagine that Huntington Bank Stadium is going to be rocking. Obviously, Minnesota not beating Michigan at home since the 70s is an alarming stat. After all, the Gophers have either been just good or dumpster fire bad since the early 1940s. Our projections have Michigan winning this game by 10 points, and it's for very good reason. However, while Michigan has the better team on paper, I feel like Minnesota is the one riding the momentum. That's why I'm taking the points with the Gophers. Chirp me on X if you must, because if this doesn't hit, I at least want to feel something. Pick: Minnesota +5.5

The Wolverines (3-1, 0-1 Big Ten) head on the road for the first time this season to face a 3-1 Minnesota team coming off an impressive road victory over Washington. Nevertheless, oddsmakers still view the Wolverines as a solid favorite. They have history on their side, too. The Wolverines have dominated the Little Brown Jug rivalry, winning 27 of the past 29 meetings and not losing in Minneapolis since 1977. Can they continue that success and bounce back in a big way? For Saturday's Big Ten clash between Michigan and Minnesota, the over/under is set at 43.5 total points on Polymarket . Also, make sure to check out our guide to the best Michigan sportsbook promos to shop for odds. Here are score predictions from MLive's beat writers: What a bizarre start to the season. Michigan finds itself 3-1 but this feels like a second "bounce back" game. With a bye looming, the Wolverines desperately need a win in Minneapolis. The good news? Michigan is coming off a largely well-played game … the defense pitched a shutout through three quarters while the offense showed serious strides moving the football. I expect more of the same on Saturday against a Golden Gophers team that wants to be balanced and play it safe. I'm not expecting all will be cured, but I do expect Michigan to have more firepower and enough explosive plays to come away with a win. Michigan 24, Minnesota 17 After letting what looked like a sure win against Iowa slip away last week, expect the Wolverines to play a more complete game against a Minnesota team they hold a clear talent advantage over. The Gophers' front seven is legitimate, led by preseason Defensive Player of the Year Anthony Smith, so generating consistent production on the ground may not come easy. Still, I think Bryce Underwood builds on last week's performance and continues to lean on his two favorite targets, Andrew Marsh and JJ Buchanan. Look for Michigan to bottle up Minnesota's rushing attack and force Drake Lindsey into a few costly mistakes through the air. The Wolverines win the game and the turnover battle, bringing the Little Brown Jug back to Ann Arbor. Michigan 27, Minnesota 17 Michigan's offense should continue its upward trajectory Saturday and find the end zone a few times. The defense might have a little more trouble than last week: Lindsey is efficient if not explosive and Minnesota has a stable of capable running backs. Michigan has questions along the offensive line but still has Bryce Underwood, Andrew Marsh, and JJ Buchanan. They've played in harsh environments — Michigan visited Oklahoma, Nebraska, and Michigan State last season, winning twice — and shouldn't be intimidated by (checks notes) Huntington Bank Stadium. Michigan's win streak at Minnesota is remarkable. It predates P.J. Fleck's existence. Continuing that streak won't be easy. I expect Saturday's game to come down to the final minutes. Will it be decided on the final play , as two of Michigan's games have already? I guess we'll find out. He was unable to get up as the Hawkeyes were rushing to the line of scrimmage to try and get off a final snap and the officials had to blow the whistle for an injury timeout. His diagnosis is unclear, but he is coming back from a notable injury after missing the end of the 2025 season and rehabbing all offseason from an Achilles. He has 16 tackles and a team-high three sacks through four weeks. For the second week in a row, his running mate, Nichols, is on the list. The junior edge was able to play against Iowa and his injury is also undisclosed. He's second on the team with 2½ sacks and is a key force on U-M's front. On offense, the most notable name is Marsh. The sophomore wideout has found his form the past two weeks, hauling in 17 total catches and more than 100 yards in each of those contests. He's made a number of highlight reel catches, including toe-taps along the sideline and one-handed snags. He's a fixture in Michigan's attack, having played 215 snaps and leading the team with 22 receptions. His name is also the biggest surprise, given he didn't show any obvious sign of injury last week, though he did at one point walk up the sideline and take off his helmet before momentarily sitting on a stationary bike. Sprague is the least surprising. He missed the past two weeks for unknown reasons and earlier this week Kyle Whittingham said the team was closer to learning the severity of his situation. While any of the four could play, evidence suggests at this point Sprague is the least likely to suit up. "I'd like to think he's going to play, but I've been fooled before," Harding said. home.headline: Michigan Hit With Major Injury Concerns Before Minnesota Showdown
home.blurb: The Wolverines ' initial availability report ahead of Saturday's Little Brown Jug matchup against Minnesota includes several important starters, with wide receiver Andrew Marsh , edge rushers John Henry Daley and Dom Nichols, and offensive tackle Andrew Sprague all listed as questionable. According to the initial Big Ten availability report , six Wolverines are questionable entering the week: Marsh, Daley, Nichols, Sprague, Manuel Beigel and Houston Ka'aha'aina-Torres. Michigan also has six players listed as out: Braydon Alford, Andrew Babalola , Jonathan Brown, Ace Hamilton, Julius Holly and Micah Ka'apana. There is at least some good news. Starting tackle Blake Frazier is probable after getting banged up against Iowa, while Jordan Marshall no longer appears on the injury report. Daley suffered a lower-body injury late against Iowa and is questionable. Whittingham provided at least one encouraging sign Monday night on the "Inside Michigan Football " radio show, saying Daley was walking without a boot or crutches. "He's walking, which is a positive, without a boot, without crutches," Whittingham said. "But we'll have to see as the week progresses how much soreness we can get out of that injury and get him back on the field." Daley has recorded 16 tackles , 4.5 tackles for loss and a team-leading three sacks this season. Nichols, meanwhile, leads Michigan with 12 pressures and is also questionable, meaning the Wolverines could potentially enter Minneapolis without both of their primary edge rushers. Offensively, Sprague remains questionable after missing the Iowa game with an injury , while Beigel's move from out last week to questionable provides at least some reason for optimism. If Marsh, Daley and Nichols are all available, Michigan heads to Minneapolis looking considerably more like the team Whittingham expected to have. If the Iowa Hawkeyes want to knock off Ohio State, things are going to have to break their way, but they also have to do their part in managing this game perfectly. It isn't just hoping to get the right bounce of the ball or be on the receiving end of a tipped pass like last week against Michigan. Skip to main content SI.COM 2025 Football Bracket Buckeyes In the NFL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BUCKEYES BB The Ohio State Buckeyes were in cruise control, dominating the Illinois Fighting Illini with a 42-19 thumping in Columbus last Saturday. The victory was enough for the Illini to dismiss their defensive coordinator, Bobby Hauck, in a mutual parting of ways. Now No. 5 Ohio State turns its attention to a ranked-vs.-ranked matchup with the No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes. The Buckeyes (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) are visiting their first hostile Big Ten environment at Kinnick Stadium, which will have much fanfare as College GameDay returns to Iowa City for a highly anticipated reunion. The game marks Ohio State’s first true Big Ten road test, as the Hawkeyes (4-0, 1-0 Big Ten) railed to secure a 20-19 last-second win over the Michigan Wolverines in Week 4. So far, the Ohio State on SI staff has hit more than 70 percent of its predictions this season. Can we see more of the same come Saturday? Check out our picks below to find out more. Ohio State vs. Iowa Game Details & Predictions Oct 5, 2024; Columbus, OH, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day shakes hands with Iowa Hawkeyes head coach Kirk Ferentz following the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium. Ohio State won 35-7. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Date: Saturday, Oct. 3 Date: Saturday, Oct. 3 Time: 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT TV Channel: CBS (consult TV Guide or preferred streaming provider for details). Odds: Ohio State -14 ; over/under is 45.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook) Location : Kinnick Stadium – Iowa City, Iowa Ohio State’s record under Ryan Day : 85-13 (8-6 in postseason bowl games/CFP). Last time vs. Iowa: A 35-7 home win on Saturday, Oct. 5, 2024. The game marks the 21st all-time meeting between the two programs, with the Buckeyes winning 17 of those matchups since Nov. 1989. Pregame festivities: College GameDay will be on-site in Iowa City for the first time since 2006. Ohio State so far this season: 3-1 (1-0 Big Ten) Zain Bando : 4-0 Dylan Buganski: 3-1 Rafael Zamorano : 3-1 Chip Minnich: 2-0 (began contributing ahead of Week 3) Zain Bando: Ohio State 38, Iowa 21 Ohio State’s first conference road game is a big one. Iowa has gotten off to a fast start behind a stingy defense, an ever-improving offensive line, plus has maintained the excellence that one would expect from a Kirk Ferentz team. Ferentz admitted this week that his team must play as close to flawless football as possible. That’s easier said than done when examining Ohio State. The Buckeyes have rolled all but one opponent (the Texas Longhorns) offensively, and even then, they had a 20-point lead in the fourth quarter before the defense collapsed, leading to a stunner in Austin nearly a month ago in a one-point loss. If Ohio State can get into an early rhythm, it should be an exciting afternoon with plenty of points and key defensive stops at the Hawkeyes’ expense, leading to a huge road win to begin a gauntlet stretch of Big Ten football. Chip Minnich: Ohio State 31, Iowa 17 Look for a slugfest. Put it another way - Iowa is going to make sure Ohio State is "Iowaed" by the time this game concludes. Longtime Iowa defensive coordinator Phil Parker will do whatever he can to eliminate explosive plays like the kind Illinois gave up to Ohio State last week, so that is going to require Ohio State offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and Coach Ryan Day to become creative with other outlets on the Ohio State offense. While it may not be pretty, and it may be stress-inducing, I like Ohio State to pull away in the fourth quarter. Rafael Zamorano: Ohio State 34, Iowa 24 The No. 5-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes are facing more than just a trap game for their Saturday date with the Iowa Hawkeyes at Kinnick Stadium. This foe must be taken seriously after taking down No. 18 Michigan at Ann Arbor last weekend. Luckily for the Buckeyes, their best player -- wideout Jeremiah Smith -- is coming off a whale of a game, including a personal-best four touchdowns against Illinois last weekend. Quarterback Julian Sayin also had one of his finest games with the program with 367 passing yards, his second-highest total ever, and a personal record tying four touchdown passes. Iowa has recently carved out a nice little niche as a defensive back school, and this year’s roster features the versatile Zach Lutner as a wildcard that can line up pretty much anywhere, along with Deshaun Lee and Jaylen Watson out on the corners. Smith against this unit will be the matchup to follow closely. Ohio State, nonetheless, should be able to avoid the upset and keep the ball rolling, coming back from Iowa City with a victory. Dylan Buganski: Ohio State 24, Iowa 13 The last time Ohio State traveled to Kinnick Stadium to face the Kirk Ferentz-led Hawkeyes, the Buckeyes did not fare well. As I do not see this game being the prettiest victory for coach Ryan Day, it should look a lot different than what occurred on Nov. 4, 2017, when Iowa handed Ohio State its biggest loss in the last century. This should be the biggest test of consistency up to this point for quarterback Julian Sayin and this offense, as Iowa should do a much better job of keeping track of Jeremiah Smith and make Sayin able to spread the ball around to other weapons and test the offensive line in establishing a run game. Offensively, Ohio State’s defense should be able to stutter Iowa's attack. Iowa’s run game has struggled against Power 5 opponents, but so has Ohio State’s run defense. That will be a battle to watch. Also, Iowa’s offense benefits greatly from creating big-play opportunities and the Buckeyes gave up many to Illinois at home last weekend. I expect a gritty game that stays within one score heading into the fourth quarter, with Ohio State scoring early in the fourth to make it two scores, and the defense should put up a strong showing down the stretch to give Ohio State its first ranked win of the season. picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Ohio State-Iowa Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS The biggest game of the week in the Big Ten is No. 14-ranked Iowa hosting No. 5 Ohio State in Iowa City on Saturday. The Hawkeyes are traditionally tough to beat at home in Kinnick Stadium, but the Buckeyes are 17-3 all-time in the series and 6-1 vs. Iowa over the last 20 years with the lone loss in that span coming in Iowa City in 2017. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS with Ohio State (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) set as a 14-point road favorite over Iowa (4-0, 1-0), per DraftKings Sportsbook . College football analyst David Pollack broke down the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I think [Iowa] has a chance because Ohio State's defense is more gettable than they've been, but to me that means Iowa has to have some passing game, a little bit of balance, run it more than they've run it, have success and defensively hold the heck on. Like just hold on, don't give up big plays, make them get in the red zone and kick 3s," Pollack said. David Pollack Makes His Pick for Ohio State-Iowa In dissecting the matchup, Pollack focused on two key components. First, he hasn't been impressed by Ohio State's defense, which lost most of its starters from last season, including three of the top 11 picks in the NFL draft. But Pollack also doesn't know how much he trusts Iowa's offense and quarterback Hank Brown to take advantage of that. "I watched every snap of Ohio State vs. Illinois. I thought [the Buckeyes'] defense, I think they've got some guys who flash occasionally, but they gave up over 6 yards a carry to Illinois. To give up almost 200 yards rushing, this is what Iowa is, this is who they want to be -- they want to run the football," Pollack said. "... Hank Brown, he needs to make a few plays down the field. They need to be able to open it up a little bit because I know they're going to run it, and I think they can run it at a decent clip." Iowa ranks 27th nationally in rushing at 215.5 yards per game, led by Kamari Moulton (284 yards and 2 TDs on 7.3 yards per carry) with a few other running backs all contributing in significant ways. But the Hawkeyes rank just 87th in passing at 213.5 YPG while Brown has thrown for 700 yards, 5 TDs and 0 INTs. Iowa's strength, as always, is its defense, which has given up the fewest points in college football (8.0 per game) while ranking 10th at the FBS level overall (239.8 YPG). The Hawkeyes haven't yet played an offense like Ohio State's, however, shutting out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa while containing limited offenses from Iowa State and Michigan. The Buckeyes are led by two Heisman Trophy candidates in 2025 finalist Julian Sayin (1,206 passing yards, 12 TDs and 1 INT) and star wideout Jeremiah Smith (33 catches for an FBS-leading 617 yards and 7 TDs). In Ohio State's Big Ten opener vs. Illinois last week, a 42-19 win, Smith had 12 catches for 217 yards and 4 TDs. Jeremiah Smith just settled ALL DEBATES, he is the GREATEST WR prospect ever. • 12 receptions (career-high) • 217 receiving yards (career-high) • 4 receiving TD’s (career-high) The Buckeyes WR was UNSTOPPABLE in the GREATEST game of his career 🤯🍿 pic.twitter.com/DhJLDREfJc But Pollack wonders if the Buckeyes' lacking rushing attack (156.75 YPG, 76th nationally) is their vulnerability in a matchup like this. "With Ohio State on the other side, man, is it anybody besides Jeremiah Smith? And here's the thing with Ohio State, can they get that run game going? ... At some point in this season they're going to need to get first downs and punch it in the red zone," Pollack said. As for his ultimate prediction for the matchup, Pollack is taking the Buckeyes and sticking close to the spread set by the oddsmakers. "I think this is a phenomenal matchup. I think Iowa is going to keep it close," he said. "If you weren't watching last week, Illinois kept it close. Illinois was very much in the game until the very last little bit, but they were still very much in striking distance. I think this is 27-13 type of a deal. "I don't think Iowa's offense is good enough. ... It's all about the offense because I think they can hang on long enough, make them kick a few field goals to stay in the game, but the [arrow points toward] Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin."
