picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Ohio State-Iowa Winner as College GameDay Heads to Kinnick Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy picked a winner for No. 5 Ohio State at No. 14 Iowa, a Week 5 Big Ten showdown that brings College GameDay to Iowa City for the first time in 20 years. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy took the Buckeyes to win 24-14 on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. He said Iowa's defense will keep the game close for a half before wide receiver Jeremiah Smith takes over. "Kinnick will be rocking," McElroy said. "I just don't know if Iowa has the downfield passing attack to punish a defense that's going to be squatting all game long on the run game." McElroy ranked Ohio State No. 1 in his preseason top 10 in August. The Buckeyes have since lost 24-23 at Texas, but they're 1-0 in Big Ten play, the same as the unbeaten Hawkeyes. Why did McElroy pick Ohio State? Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) scores a touchdown | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Smith, a junior, caught 12 passes for 217 yards and four touchdowns in a 42-19 win over Illinois last week. His four scores tied the Ohio State single-game record, and he became the first Buckeye with 3,000 career receiving yards. Quarterback Julian Sayin threw for 367 yards against the Illini, and McElroy said Ohio State's 11 yards per pass attempt ranks second in the country. "If Smith gets to 100 yards, you feel pretty confident about Ohio State winning the game," McElroy said. McElroy said Ohio State is 63-1 under head coach Ryan Day when it runs for more than 150 yards. Iowa allows just 88 rushing yards per game, though. The Hawkeyes average 6.5 yards per carry, and running back Kamari Moulton leads the team with 284 yards. Illinois gained 462 yards on the Buckeyes last week, the most Ohio State has allowed since Oregon put up 496 in October 2024. Since 2005, Iowa head coach Kirk Ferentz is 118-37 when his team throws fewer than 30 passes, according to McElroy. Quarterback Hank Brown hasn't thrown an interception this season, and he beat Michigan with a 16-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Reece Vander Zee as time expired. "Count Brown's pass attempts," McElroy said. "If it gets anywhere near 30, then Ohio State has probably taken the run game away, and then it's chase mode for Iowa, which is a really bad recipe." My Ohio State vs. Iowa prediction and college football picks expect Ryan Day's offense to expose an overrated Hawkeyes team. TOP PICK Who will win Ohio State vs Iowa today? Pick: Ohio State -14.5 This is Ryan Day's third time leading Ohio State against Iowa since taking over the Buckeyes in 2019. In the previous two matchups, the Buckeyes beat the Hawkeyes 54-10 as a 30-point favorite and 35-7 as a 17.5-point favorite. Another Ohio State blowout is brewing in a huge letdown spot for Iowa (I like the Buckeyes to cover -14.5 or better ). While the Hawkeyes are coming off a last-second win over Michigan and have College GameDay in town for the first time in 20 years, their win over the Wolverines is misleading. Bryce Underwood had one of the best games of his career against Iowa (three big-time throws, zero turnover-worthy plays), and if Michigan hadn't come away with no points on two drives that ended inside Iowa's 20, the Wolverines would have won. Ohio State has no trouble finishing drives, ranking No. 13 nationally in points per opportunity (5.11) and No. 7 in offensive success rate (52.4%) . That's going to be a massive problem against an Ohio State aerial assault that's among the best in college football. Led by Julian Sayin (his 92.8 QBR is No. 2 in the country) and Heisman Trophy odds- favorite Jeremiah Smith , Ohio State ranks fourth nationally in EPA per pass and third in pass success rate (60.9%). Best Ohio State vs Iowa props Prop pick #1: DJ Vonnahme Over 28.5 receiving yards DJ Vonnahme is next up at Tight End U, so this receiving line is disrespecting his talents a bit. He's off to a "slow" start to the season, but that's more injury-related than anything. He returned to the field last week against Michigan and caught four passes for 44 yards. The opportunity and talent are there for Ja'Kobi to have yet another productive day on the ground. The market is overrating Bo since he's the household name, but Ja'Kobi has had the better analytics thus far and is firmly entrenched in a valuable role. Prop pick #3: Kamari Moulton Over 13.5 rushing attempts Iowa will need to establish the run to control the ball, the clock, and this game. The Hawkeyes can't compete score-for-score with Ohio State and Jeremiah Smith if this game turns into a shootout, and the coaching staff knows it. That'll mean a healthy dose of Kamari Moulton . Iowa's RB1 had just 13 carries a week ago, but it was encouraging that none of his backups saw more than four totes. LJ Phillips Jr. was brought in from the FCS level after rushing for nearly 2,000 yards a season ago. If Timmons is unable to return against the Hawkeyes, coach Ryan Day mentioned as cornerbacks Jermaine Mathews Jr. and Jordan Thomas as other options to take over for him in the slot. The statuses of starting right tackle Phillip Daniels and tight end Bennett Christian are also uncertain this week. They were both listed as questionable. Daniels has been sidelined since the loss at Texas , prompting the Buckeyes to reconfigure the right side of the offensive line. Austin Siereveld has started the last two games at right tackle with Gabe VanSickle at right guard. Christian was out last week against Illinois. The conference’s availability report does not specify the nature of the injuries. The Buckeyes could see the return of starting defensive end Zion Grady, who was left off the report after missing the last two games. away.headline: Ohio State's OL Starts to Take Shape As Phillip Daniels Remains Questionable
away.blurb: Ohio State's OL Starts to Take Shape As Phillip Daniels Remains Questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF The prospect of losing your job thanks to injury is a frustrating reality that might be taking place inside the Ohio State program. Right tackle Phillip Daniels showed up on today's injury report as questionable for their game against Iowa, and he is now in danger of missing his fourth straight football game. Unfortunately, his being out has opened the door for what might end up being a total changeover on the Buckeyes' offensive line. IN his absence, the Buckeyes have inserted Ian Moore at left tackle, Gabe Van Sickle at right guard, and then Austin Siereveld moves back to right tackle. The final injury report will come out closer to game time, but it is more than likely that Daniels is going to be down. If that does end up being the case, pay close attention to the performance up front and what the Buckeyes are able to do against what will be the second-best DL that they will face. Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads These guys filled in around the two stalwarts inside of Luke Montgomery and Carson Hinzman, who have been rock solid all year long. Now, the forced result of Daniels' injury is the development of these young players up front. They have been required to get better and haven't had any other option. Now, the Buckeyes as a team are faced with what Ryan Day refers to as a good problem, that they now have great depth up front. Ohio State Buckeyes Prepare to Invade Kinnick Stadium to Take On IowaThe Ohio State Buckeyes are preparing to head down to Iowa City to take on the Iowa Hawkeyes in their second biggest challenge to date. We learned a lot from... The other result, more specifically for Daniels , is that as each week goes by, he loses reps and the guys up front build on the chemistry that they have been developing. That's never a good way to potentially lose a job or even find yourself in a competition for the position. Ever hear of Wally Pip? Back to what this means for the Buckeyes. I couldn't agree more with Ryan Day on this: the Buckeyes now have six or seven guys that they trust to put in. Furthermore, Austin Siereveld has now shown that he can play quite literally every single position on the offensive line. This is great insurance for injury; this is great insurance for poor play. We have seen plenty of that over the past two seasons, and n ow Day and offensive line coach Tyler Bowen will have something to combat that. Best case scenario for the Buckeyes is that Daniels is back soon. If he isn't, they will have plenty of solutions to patchwork that group together.

picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS College football analyst Greg McElroy has made his pick for No. 8 Florida at No. 25 Missouri. The ESPN host sees running back Jadan Baugh and the Gators' ground game as the biggest problem for a Tigers team that just lost its conference opener. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. Missouri slid from No. 19 to No. 25 after it gave up the last 14 points in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. "So, for Missouri, this is got-to-have-it mode, given what's coming up here in the next few weeks," McElroy said. McElroy has liked this Florida team since the summer , when he said the Gators could play spoiler in the 2026 Playoff race. How can Missouri slow Jadan Baugh? Vernell Brown III leads the team with 17 catches for 271 yards , and Florida head coach Jon Sumrall said the knee injury Brown suffered against Ole Miss is a mild strain . picks.headline: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri
picks.blurb: David Pollack Picks Winner of Florida-Missouri Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS A week ago, Florida was the team in prime position to deliver an upset while playing at home against an opponent, Ole Miss, that was coming off a huge win the previous week. The role is reversed in Week 5 for the No. 8-ranked Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC), who delivered their statement with a 52-28 win over that then-top-5 Rebels team and now must avoid a letdown of their own on the road against No. 25 Missouri (3-1, 0-1). Florida is set as a 5.5-point road favorite, per DraftKings Sportsbook , in a matchup that kicks off at 3:30 p.m. ET Saturday on ABC. College football analyst David Pollack dissected the matchup on his "See Ball Get Ball" podcast. Alabama-Mississippi State, Ohio State-Iowa, Florida-Missouri AND MORE Week 5 CFB Picks https://t.co/8vWS9mTHpm "I want to be Missouri so bad in this matchup because everybody, everybody is like 'Oh, this Buster Faulkner guy's good. This Jon Sumrall guy's good!'" Pollack said of Florida's much ballyhooed new offensive coordinator and head coach. "We've been talking about it for a while -- welcome aboard everybody. "Here's the thing why this matchup becomes really awesome. You have that going for you, again, just like [with Florida vs. Ole Miss] last week, Missouri is playing at home. Florida is not sneaking up on anybody, right?" David Pollack Makes His Prediction For Florida-Missouri Pollack explained why he believes Missouri can potentially be a tough matchup for the Gators and what the Tigers are going to need to do to pull the upset. To put it simply, that requires slowing down running backs Jadan Baugh (600 rushing yards and 11 TDs on 7.2 yards per carry) and Duke Clark (259 yards and 3 TDs on 8.1 YPC) and a Florida rushing attack that ranks 11th nationally at 260.0 YPG while forcing quarterback Aaron Philo to make more plays with his arm. Philo, the Georgia Tech transfer who followed Faulker to Florida and is in his first season as a starter, has only attempted 87 passes in four games for 917 yards, 7 TDs and 2 INTs. Philo was 16-of-23 passing for 196 yards, 1 TD and 0 INTs plus a rushing TD in the win over Ole Miss. "Missouri's defense, watching them vs. Mississippi State, Missouri's defense always finds a way to be physical, they always find a way to be good in the front 7. They can rush the passer, 10 coming off the edge is consistently a problem," Pollack said of edge rusher Daeden Hopkins, who has 6 sacks and 2 forced fumbles already. "... Here's what I'm interested to see, this is the only thing that matters to me, can you put it in Philo's hands? Like literally, at some point who can make Philo be a QB because right now -- and I'm not knocking Philo, they're doing what they need to do and they're undefeated -- but right now Philo is getting worn out by handing that thing off. "Over 300 [rushing yards] a game the last two games against Auburn and Ole Miss. That is a feat, that is impressive. The offensive line is impressive. The system is impressive. Who is going to be the first to say, 'Philo, you've got to beat me'? And can he go through progressions and make those plays when it's not the easy stuff. Can you take away the layups, get him off schedule a little bit? If Missouri can do that at home, that will be interesting for me to watch. That's what I'm looking for the most in this game." Missouri lost its SEC opener 31-24 at Mississippi State last week and has played only one other Power 4 teams so far (a 38-21 win at Kansas). The Tigers are led by quarterback Austin Simmons, the Ole Miss transfer who has passed for 947 yards, 11 TDs and 0 INTs so far. Jamal Roberts (395 rushing yards and 3 TDs on 4.4 YPC) leads the rushing attack, that is still waiting for star Ahmad Hardy to return as he continues to recover and work back from an offseason gunshot wound. Ultimately, Pollack is picking the Gators to win by a comfortable margin. He's a believer in what Sumrall has built in his first season at Florida. "I trust Florida by this point now, I do. I trust them," Pollack said. "I will say this, Florida's receiving corps is banged up to heck. It's going to be very interesting to watch them. I've got Florida 38, Missouri 27ish. I'm trusting Florida on the road after a big game." Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Florida vs Missouri Odds Florida vs Missouri Spread : Florida -4.5 (-115), Missouri +4.5 (-105) Florida vs Missouri Over/Under : 56.5 (-115o / -105u) Florida vs Missouri Moneyline : Florida -210, Missouri +172 I love first-year Florida head coach John Sumrall, who instantly turned the Gators into a national title contender in his first season in Gainesville. After leading Tulane to the College Football Playoff in 2025, the Gators came knocking with a big contract offer for Sumrall, given how poorly Florida had been for several years under Billy Napier. Florida has been spectacular in just four games under Sumrall. Its offense is averaging over 53 points per game despite facing several difficult SEC foes, including Auburn and Ole Miss . Gators quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 917 yards over Florida's first four contests and ranks inside the top 15 in the country with an 85.4 QBR. Florida boasts a loaded offensive unit, primarily led by tailback Jadan Baugh, who has quickly established himself as not just one of the best running backs in college football, but as one of the premier overall players in the nation. Baugh has rushed for an incredible 600 yards over the Gators' first four games and has already found the end zone 11 times, ranking second and first nationally, respectively. Florida's receiving corps has been quite impressive as well. Sophomore wideouts Vernell Brown III and Dallas Wilson have both racked up at least 235 receiving yards on the season. In addition to Sumrall's Gators ranking second in college football with 53.5 points per game, Florida's defense is allowing less than 23 points per game heading into Week 5's SEC showdown. Florida's stop unit has also been under a new regime in 2026, with former Kentucky defensive coordinator Brad White installing multi-faceted three-man and four-man fronts that largely focus on stopping the run, generating pressure, and minimizing explosive plays. While the Gators travel to Austin to play top-ranked Texas in two weeks, Florida will by no stretch of the imagination overlook Saturday's difficult road test against a ranked conference foe in Missouri. While Missouri is coming off its first loss of the 2026 season after falling to Mississippi State by a touchdown, the Tigers will be very motivated heading back home to Columbia for a tough Week 5 matchup against the undefeated Gators. Missouri signed head coach Eli Drinkwitz to a six-year contract worth upwards of $10 million annually after the former SEC Coach of the Year led his Tigers to 10 wins in 2023 and again in 2024. Tigers quarterback Austin Simmons has been phenomenal over his first four games as Missouri's QB1 after riding the bench at Ole Miss for two seasons. Simmons has thrown for an impressive 947 yards in the air and 11 touchdowns without throwing a single interception over his first four games in Columbia. Unfortunately for Mizzou's offense, star tailback Ahmad Hardy remains with no timetable for return after ranking second in all of college football with 1,649 rushing yards in 2025. Despite Hardy's absence, the Tigers have still been pretty effective in their rushing attack, with backups Jamal Roberts and Xai'Shaun Edwards carrying the load for Mizzou's backfield in impressive fashion. Missouri boasts an elite receiving corps as well, led by senior wide receiver Cayden Lee , who has already racked up 412 receiving yards to rank ninth in the country. As two former Rebels, Lee and Simmons have quickly re-established their chemistry and have formed a very dangerous connection that has given opposing defenses nightmares. Drinkwitz continues to run a versatile power spread offense using heavy tight end formations to balance short-yardage pounding with perimeter passing, which has led to an uptempo Tiger offense scoring over 35 points per game thus far. Missouri's defensive unit has been quite impressive as well, giving up less than 21 points per game thus far. Senior linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. has been the anchor for the Tigers' elite front seven. If the Tigers are to pull off the upset in Saturday's SEC clash, it will undoubtedly require a massive effort from this Mizzou defense. We're in for a great matchup on Saturday afternoon between two SEC foes off to promising starts in their respective 2026 campaigns. While I have been very impressed by Missouri's level of play over its first four games, the Tigers must face an uptempo Gators offense that ranks second nationally in points scored this season. Though I definitely expect the Tigers to hang around early, I love Florida in this spot and feel confident backing Sumrall's Gators to cover the 4.5-point spread. Picks: Florida -4.5 (-115)

Heisman hopeful running back Jadan Baugh has been an absolute machine this season, and the Gators are hoping that stays the same here in this one. Quarterback Aaron Philo will likely be without his leading receiver , but Missouri lost a pair of difference-making EDGE rushers, so there's still plenty of room for the Gators offense to look as good as ever. away.headline: Florida football injury update: VBIII, Bailey Stockton questionable for Mizzou
away.blurb: News Sports Opinion Guardian Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update: VBIII, Bailey Stockton questionable for Mizzou Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Sept. 30, 2026, 8:53 p.m. ET Florida football wide receivers Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton have been listed as questionable for UF's game at No. 25 Missouri (October 3, 3:30 p.m., ABC) on the SEC's Initial Availability Report released on September 30. Brown III suffered a knee injury after an 11-yard run in the second quarter during UF's 52-28 win over Ole Miss and did not return. Stockton, meanwhile, suffered a back injury on a helmet-to-helmet targeting hit by Ole Miss safety Joenel Arguero, who was ejected on the play. He returned to field punts in the second half but has been limited in practice this week. If Stockton and Brown are both out, Florida could turn to receivers Eric Singleton Jr., Kahleil Jackson and Micah Mays Jr. for more snaps against Missouri. Singleton returned to the field after sitting out two-plus game with an ankle injury and caught a 38-yard pass against Ole Miss, while also forcing a pass interference penalty. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy, the SEC's leading rusher from 2025 with 1,649 yards, remains out while recovering from a gunshot wound in his leg. Also out for the Tigers (3-1, 0-1 SEC) are safety, JaDon Blair, running back Malae Fonoti, offensive lineman Josh Atkins and tight end Gavin Hoffman. Edge rushers Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith and linebacker Bobby Washington Jr. are questionable for Missouri. Brown leads the No. 8 Florida Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) in receiving with 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 TDs. He's also been a weapon on special teams with two punt returns for TDs. Stockton, meanwhile, has 13 catches for 106 yards and 1 TD on the season. Florida football may need to turn to depth at WR "He played 8-9 snaps," said Florida football offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner, who coached Singleton at Georgia Tech. "He went deep three or four; he got a pass interference; he got the 38-yard gain. So, yeah, he brings a totally different element when it comes to being able to take the top off of defense than really anybody I've ever been around." UF has been relatively healthy so far under first-year coach Jon Sumrall, in part due to a strength and conditioning program under Rusty Whitt that focuses on building strength for injury prevention. Whitt is having players maintain a strict weight room schedule during the regular season. "We've put a lot of work in," Sumrall said. "You know, things that are strong are resilient and don't break easily. So there's a lot of work that's been put in by Rusty (Whitt) and Paul Silvestri and that group. Very grateful for our sports medicine team and strength staff, they all do a phenomenal job." Kevin Brockway is The Gainesville Sun’s Florida beat writer. Contact him at kbrockway@gannett.com. Follow him on X @KevinBrockwayG1.

An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, there are two major factors that make it essentially impossible for Florida State to win. The Seminoles have the ACC's second-worst pass defense through four games — so Virginia should have little trouble scoring 35-plus points. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. The Cavaliers can capitalize on those turnovers by turning them into lengthy touchdown drives. Florida State is capable of making things interesting — especially at home — but there are a few reasons why Virginia is the favorite in an ACC road game. picks.headline: Three bold predictions for Virginia at Florida State
picks.blurb: This afternoon, the Cavaliers will fight for their fourth win of the 2026 season. This could be a crucial one. The ACC is much deeper than years past — which makes every conference game even more important than usual. Even one loss can put a team just a hair away from being eliminated from the ACC title race. Here are three bold predictions as Virginia aims to keep pace with the other undefeated ACC title hopefuls. Duce Robinson hits 175 receiving yards against Virginia Coach Tony Elliott said he considers Duce Robinson the best wide receiver in the ACC. Robinson might very well have a case for that title. At the minimum, the Cavaliers know that he can carry an offense. Robinson had 147 yards and a touchdown against Virginia last season. This year, the Cavaliers are still figuring out their cornerback play. Ja'Son Prevard, Emmanuel Karnley and Jordan Robinson made big plays against the Seminoles in 2025 but all three are gone. One new starter is Jacobie Henderson, who has been torched for several catches of 10-plus yards, even against mid-major opponents. If Florida State can scheme the 6-foot-6 Robinson up against the 5-foot-11 Henderson, he might top 100 yards in just a few drives. Beau Pribula throws for 350 yards Florida State currently has the second-worst pass defense in the ACC. It is entirely possible Beau Pribula dices up a mediocre secondary, especially now that top receiver Rico Flores Jr. is healthy enough to carry a bigger workload. The Seminoles have been decent against the run — which also means that a passing frenzy could be in the cards. Pribula has been one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the country. If he gets enough passing attempts, he should be able to hit the mark of 350 yards. Pribula probably would have gotten there at least once already this season if he was not pulled with a huge lead and a few quarters left to play. The Cavaliers score their first defensive touchdown of the season Virginia has forced seven turnovers in its first four games. However, none of those turnovers have been returned for touchdowns. Linebacker Kam Robinson almost had a pick-six against Delaware, but he dropped the ball. The Seminoles have been quite turnover-prone thus far. More likely than not, the Cavaliers will snatch at least one turnover. Robinson or safety Brandyn Hillman might take one to the house today. Virginia vs. Florida State Pick: Virginia -2.5 My Florida State vs. Virginia best bet is on the Cavaliers to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Virginia vs Florida State Odds Virginia vs Florida State point spread : Virginia -2.5 (-115), Florida State +2.5 (-105) Virginia vs Florida State over/under : 51.5 (-108o / -114u) Virginia vs Florida State moneyline : Virginia -145, Florida State +120 What a start to the season Virginia quarterback Beau Pribula is having, don't you think? He's playing to a wonderful 11-to-1 touchdown -to-interception ratio, while completing 76.7% of his passes. Do I think those numbers are sustainable? Probably not, but it's still worth mentioning. The one thing that I worry about him, though, is how often he's been sacked. Virginia's offensive line has been a sieve, ranking in the bottom 20 in sack percentage and letting opposing defenses get to its quarterbacks nine total times. And this is a team that primarily likes to run the ball. The Cavaliers are ranked 74th in pass attempts per game, while ranking eighth in rushing attempts. So, yes, there's concern there, because there's nothing spectacular about Virginia's run game. It likes to split the ball between a running back committee because Jekail Middlebrook hasn't separated himself from the pack. Middlebrook hasn't proven to be an effective distance runner, and Xay Davis and Xavier Brown clearly have the efficiency edge. On another note, I really like what the Cavs are doing defensively. They have a deadly secondary led by Jacobie Henderson and Brandyn Hillman. Hillman has already recorded three interceptions and a forced fumble. Not only that, Virginia is one of the best teams in standard down metrics, ranking second in explosiveness allowed and eighth in PPA. Its work against the pass is unsurprisingly its best attribute with Henderson and Hillman, and the Cavs rank fifth in PPA allowed and 10th in success rate allowed. Color me confused on these Seminoles. They're one of the most difficult teams to read in this Group of 6. They started off the season awfully slow against New Mexico State , despite winning, and then got into a slugfest against both SMU and Alabama. And at one point, it seemed like FSU was poised to beat Alabama for the second consecutive season, this time in Tuscaloosa. Quarterback Ashton Daniels seemed like he was lost in the pocket after the first two weeks, played a strong first half against Bama, then threw three interceptions against the Tide. The following week, he threw another pick against Central Arkansas, no less. This is a boom-or-bust team. There's a reason why the Noles have one of the most explosive offenses in the FBS, yet sit 11th in the ACC . Running back Ousmane Kromah has been a star, rushing for 6.4 yards per catch and five touchdowns. Receivers Duce Robinson and Jayvan Boggs are big-time playmakers, but because Daniels is so volatile, they can't be a big part of the offense. Defensively, this is a squad that has some active hands. Currently, 11 players have recorded a pass breakup, including two each from defensive backs Ja'Bril Rawls and Ma'Khi Jones. However, that's all the nice things you'll hear from me about their defense. Florida State ranks near the bottom in nearly every standard down metric. I'm inclined to take Virginia here. Simply, I'm riding with the better team. While this game is being played in Tallahassee, I don't think the Seminoles are good enough defensively to stop the Cavaliers. That's not to say Virginia is perfect, but because Florida State has such a hard time defensively, I see Virginia's offensive line using this game as a "get right" moment. The one concern I have with picking the Cavs is the Daniels factor. He's been known to take off and run. In Virginia's sole loss against West Virginia, the Cavs got chewed up badly by dual-threat quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr., and I can definitely see Daniels using that to his advantage. If Virginia can learn from that loss and not make the same mistakes, this is a prime opportunity to lay the points with the Cavaliers. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. The season is on the verge of running off the tracks and the result of this game could smooth things out for another week or completely derail the entire season. Who comes out on top in a battle between former SEC East foes? South Carolina is in the midst of an eight game losing streak to Power Four opponents, which includes seven losses to SEC teams. During this losing streak Beamer's Gamecocks have fallen to Alabama (twice), LSU, Oklahoma, Mississippi State, Texas A&M, and Ole Miss. Their last win came against Kentucky in a 35-13 route of the Wildcats. However now with Will Stein at the helm, this is not the same Kentucky team of recent years. Wildcats QB Kenny Minchey and this offense have been very efficient and moved the ball well. They got a statement win earlier in the year at College Station and are looking for another. What may help South Carolina in this one is Kentucky's leaky defense . The Wildcats rank 14th in scoring (25 ppg), 12th in rushing (122.25 yards per game), and 13th against the pass (234 yards per game). Rain may be in the forecast for this weekend. This very well could play right into the Gamecocks' hands as they have a much improved rushing attack from last season. With that said, I believe the Gamecocks are in for a bounce back spot on Saturday. Kentucky's defense will give up plays through the air and on the ground. Kendal Briles should be able to mix up the play calling well and allow LaNorris Sellers to get into a groove. Matt Fuller has topped the 100-yard mark twice in the last three games. I believe he hits that number once again and officially puts a bad losing streak to an end. Joey Walraven: South Carolina 24, Kentucky 21 This game is a must-win for the South Carolina Gamecocks. A loss here could potentially be cement another losing season for the Gamecocks and be the final touches on Shane Beamer's exit . With those implications, I expect LaNorris Sellers to have his best game of the season and lead the Gamecocks to a hard fought victory. Sellers will cetainly need to play well, but the difference in this game will be on the ground. The duo of Jason Patterson and CJ Baxter also gives the UK offense a very formidable rushing attack — a challenge this week will be the fact that one of Kentucky's strengths runs directly into South Carolina 's strongest defensive unit. The Wildcats rank among the nation's best teams in Rushing Success Rate, but the Gamecocks have been excellent at limiting rushing efficiency, allowing opponents to stay on schedule on just 32.7% of rushing attempts. To offset this, Minchey will need to attack vertically to Kenny Darby, whose 226 receiving yards lead the team, and force South Carolina's secondary to defend explosive plays downfield. On the other side, the defensive numbers have been somewhat concerning thus far for the Wildcats. They've struggled to consistently stop the run, ranking outside the top 90 nationally in Rushing Success Rate allowed and outside the top 110 in Rush PPA allowed. Those numbers are worrisome against a South Carolina offense that will make it a point of emphasis to establish the run and also has an extremely mobile quarterback in LaNorris Sellers . Generating turnovers has helped this defense get off the field throughout September, but it's unclear if that's a sustainable formula. The Wildcats will need to lean on defensive lineman Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace, who leads the team with 2.5 sacks, to get into the backfield and pressure Sellers. I have doubts as to whether or not UK will be able to force the Gamecocks into many punting situations. It was an important year for Shane Beamer and company, and the last two weeks have caused many of the Gamecock fans to grow restless. South Carolina lost at home to Mississippi State in a game it at one point led by double digits, and then got dominated last week in Tuscaloosa by Alabama. This now feels like a do-or-die spot for Beamer's team, where it will either come out inspired in front of its home crowd and prove it still has some fight left this season, or come out lethargic and be staring three consecutive losses right in the eye. I think Beamer still has this locker room intact, so I'm betting on the former. The Gamecocks offense is still averaging 499.3 yards and 38.5 points per game while ranking among the nation's top rushing offenses at 262.0 rushing yards per contest. Sellers has been up-and-down throughout his career in Columbia, but when he has it rolling, he's one of the most talented signal-callers in America. Running back Matt Fuller is one of the more underappreciated backs in the conference and has averaged over 6.5 yards per carry thus far in the season. Kentucky's run defense will have its hands full against a Gamecock offense that can hurt you on the ground in a bunch of different ways. On the other side of the ball, there's talent but also plenty of issues. The secondary has gotten torched in recent weeks, but I don't know that the Kentucky passing attack has the firepower to exploit it as Mississippi State and Alabama did. Additionally, star edge rusher Dylan Stewart won't play due to suspension, but could that be a moment where the rest of this defense rallies together in his absence? It's certainly possible. Forcing a turnover or two would certainly go a long way in helping the Gamecocks create separation on their home field. I think this is a buy-low spot on a Gamecock team that's still more talented than Kentucky and should treat this game as a last-stand type of spot. The Kentucky win at Texas A&M looked massive at the time but has aged poorly after what the Aggies showed last week against LSU . I don't think the Kentucky defense will have an answer for Sellers and the SC offense, and while the Gamecock defense has several flaws, I've still got some faith in it to create some negative plays inside Williams-Brice Stadium. It may not be pretty, but give me South Carolina to win and cover in bounce-back mode on Saturday afternoon. Pick: South Carolina -2.5

ET on Saturday. We have previewed both South Carolina offense and defense, as well as laying out Kentucky's path to victory in this game. This is a massive game for both teams; Kentucky is trying to snap a four game losing streak against the Gamecocks and South Carolina is a desperate trying to turnaround their season. In this article, I will give my final thoughts on the game and a prediction. Kentucky has to win early downs in this game, and they have consistently done that all season on both sides of the football. Kentucky's offense has stayed ahead of schedule consistently and haven't needed to rely on converting third downs, which has been a weak spot for this offense. Kentucky's offensive line has improved every week and they have to dominate the line of scrimmage in this game. They have been phenomenal in run blocking as they lead the country in yards before contact per rush attempt, and they should keep Kenny Minchey clean as South Carolina is without their game-wrecking edge defender Dylan Stewart. Defensively, Kentucky has performed similarly as the offense. They are struggling on third downs, but they have been exceptional on early downs. If they can slow down this South Carolina run game and keep their offense off schedule, it should bode well for the Wildcats defense. Kentucky will probably have a similar defensive gameplan that they had against Texas A&M, contain LaNorris Sellers on the ground and force him to beat you with his arm. Sellers has struggled this season, he has turned the ball over four times. The turnover margin has been the downfall of Kentucky in this series as of late, as the Wildcats have 14 total turnovers in the last five matchups against the Gamecocks. That could flip on Saturday, Kentucky is +3 in the turnover margin on the season, whereas South Carolina is -4 in the turnover margin. Kentucky has done a great job at taking care of the football and creating turnovers on defense. South Carolina has their backs against the wall, head coach Shane Beamer is on a scorching hot seat. They have struggled against SEC opponents and the talk surrounding their program has been extremely loud this week. Combine that with your best player serving a suspension, it will be a lot to overcome for the Gamecocks. Who gets off to a hot start could be the determining factor in this football game. Speaking of hot starts, there are multiple reasons it could play a factor in this game. South Carolina needs to create that early momentum to keep the crowd involved. If Kentucky gets off to a hot start and the Gamecocks struggle offensively, you could see the boo birds come out in Columbia from this fan base. It is worth noting, Kentucky ranks third in the SEC this season in time trailing this season, as the Wildcats have only spent a total of over 26 minutes trailing through the first month of play. Kentucky has been good at getting off to quick starts this season, and I could see that continue on Saturday. Kentucky has a unique offensive scheme that will force a struggling South Carolina defense to communicate. Over the last five meetings, the Wildcats have averaged just 13 points per game, which is the main reason they have been 1-4 over that stretch. I believe Kentucky gets the offense going and South Carolina fails to overcome all the noise surrounding the team this week. Prediction: Kentucky 34, South Carolina 24 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at South Carolina: Final Thoughts and Prediction

Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will look to justify its No. 24 ranking at South Carolina on Saturday. The Wildcats are ranked for the first time in almost three years, but if they don't snap a four-game losing streak to the Gamecocks, the stint in The Associated Press Top 25 will not last long. Will Stein's squad has already proven capable of winning in a raucous road environment at Texas A&M, but Stein has been clear he does not believe UK's performance in a win over South Alabama last week was up to the program's standard. Can Kentucky build momentum in advance of a homecoming game against LSU? Can Stein flip the script in a series that has often gone a long way in determining the success of each team's season? Here is what you need to know ahead of the matchup . Kentucky cracked the AP Top 25 for the first time since October 2023 this week but remains in the "others receiving votes" portion of the Coaches Poll. That distinction offers a glimpse at the work the Wildcats still need to do to earn national respect. Upsetting Texas A&M put UK in the spotlight for a week, but now there are real questions about how good the Aggies are. Combine the sluggish opening to the win over South Alabama, and Kentucky's hold on a spot in the Top 25 appears tenuous. "It's cool and all, but I mean that thing shifts every single day," offensive guard Tegra Tshabola said. "We keep focusing on that, we won't be in there long." A win at South Carolina might not move the needle much in terms of national perception since the Gamecocks are 0-2 in SEC play, but it would at least ensure Kentucky remains ranked for its homecoming matchup against LSU next week. Despite UK's spot in the top 25, South Carolina is a three-point favorite as of Friday morning. "I think it's more important for the fans than anything," Stein said. "Our guys got to go play well. I'm not really sure why they rank people this early in the season. There's a lot of games left. It's about playing well on Saturdays. Not letting that dictate how we play. We should play to our standard regardless." Kentucky defensive lineman Kahlil Saunders (92) tries to wrap up South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers (16) during a game at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, S.C., on Saturday, Sept. 27, 2025. (Ryan C. Hermens/rhermens@herald-leader.com) Another test for UK defense South Carolina was blown out 49-18 at Alabama last week but averaged 45 points per game in its first three games. That stretch included a 41-34 loss to Mississippi State. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers entered the season as a top-50 NFL draft prospect, according to The Athletic, but his performance has been mixed so far. Through four games, Sellers has completed 62.1% of his passes for 833 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also rushed for 244 yards and one touchdown on 36 carries. Sellers' stats are boosted by his performance in the season-opening 57-0 win over Kent State in which he completed 19 of 23 passes for 270 yards and three touchdowns. In two SEC games, Sellers has thrown three touchdowns and three interceptions. He also completed just 10 of 23 passes for 96 yards in the Week 2 blowout of Towson but did rush for 119 yards in that game. "I think he's extremely dynamic," Stein said. "He can make every single throw. Big arm, and then when he pulls the ball down, he's very dangerous. They also have really good skill players on offense, so it'll be a big task for our defense to go against these guys, especially in their place." Sellers has given Kentucky fits the last two seasons, completing 21 of 28 passes for 319 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. He rushed for 81 yards on 14 carries last season. Kentucky football injury report Stein downplayed any long-term concerns about UK players who picked up injuries in recent weeks, but the Wildcats will be without at least one key player in Columbia. Junior wide receiver DJ Miller, who was injured while trying to run a deep route against South Alabama, was initially listed as doubtful on the SEC availability report then downgraded to out on Friday. Long snapper Cole Marszalek, backup cornerback Grant Grayton, offensive guards Jay Clark and Aba Selm and linebacker Tavion Wallace were also listed as out Fifth-year linebacker Alex Afari was also listed as unavailable Friday after the Kentucky Court of Appeals dismissed the temporary injunction that had made him and dozens of other athletes eligible in their lawsuit against the NCAA for a fifth season of eligibility. The good news for UK is star defensive tackle Tavion Gadson, who missed the South Alabama game, was not included on the availability report, signalling he is expected to play at South Carolina. Kentucky vs. South Carolina prediction A fast start could be particularly important Saturday with frustrations high among South Carolina fans. If Kentucky can take control of the game early, the atmosphere could grow tense for Shane Beamer and Gamecocks players. A high-scoring affair seems likely, but Kentucky's experience at Texas A&M should help prepare the Wildcats for the moment. Kentucky 35, South Carolina 28. The last word "I don't know a stadium in this league that's not going to be loud. … I would imagine every stadium we go into is going to have crazy fans that are really passionate and make third downs and fourth downs really difficult on the opposing offense. So, it goes back to how do you play good football? Learn how to not beat yourself before you go in. Have to be elite in communication, in operation, in and out of huddles. No huddles, cadence, all that stuff is going to be critical for our success. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Alex Joyce Fri, October 2, 2026 at 6:17 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Despite all the troubles from the last two weeks, South Carolina has a chance to get the train back on the track against Kentucky. For a team desparately needing a win, here are three bold predicitions for the Gamecocks that will ultimately end their 2-game skid this season. Usually we try to give you at least one on each side of the ball, however this week we're changing things up. This is an all offense version of bold predictions. We will focus on LaNorris Sellers, the passing game, and the tailbacks. Passing Game looks smooth again It certainly won't be easy. Though Knetucky's "stats" place them in the bottom half of SEC defenses in the passing category, it doesn't tell the full story. In two SEC games the Wildcats held Alabama's Keelon Russell to 188 yards passing and Texas A&M's Marcel Reed to 236 yards. They also lead the conference in interceptions with 6. What gives me confidence in this specific matchup will be South Carolina's ability to run the ball (more on that later). A good run game can open passing windows for an offense that has struggled in that department for the last two weeks. I expect this to be the case and for Gamecocks to see a better attack than they have in recent weeks. This is a front seven that can be run on and that's exactly what this Gamecocks' offense does best. Matt Fuller leads a rushing attack that is ranked first in the conference with 262 yards per game. Fuller gained 112 yards on the ground last week as the team put up 216 yards total on Alabama. Against Mississippi State running backs totaled 149 yards. That's good enough for 182.5 yards per game through two contests. Fuller should have his third 100 yard rushing performance of the season which will propel the Gamecocks to a win. While the hype and excitement are there, the Wildcats have a big-time game on Saturday on the road against the South Carolina Gamecocks. This is a big weekend for both Stein and Beamer, but Kentucky fans are hoping the Wildcats will be heading back home with a big-time win. Miami enters 4-0 and 2-0 in the ACC, while Clemson sits at 3-1 and 2-0 in conference play. The Tigers have won three straight since getting embarrassed 51-10 by LSU in the opener, including a 24-10 road win over Cal last week. But Clemson hasn't faced anything quite like this Miami team since that LSU disaster. The Hurricanes are averaging 51.8 points and 588.8 yards per game , ranking first nationally in total offense. Even scarier, Miami's defense is allowing only 9.0 points and 224.5 yards per game . How Miami Wins It starts with Darian Mensah . Mensah has been ridiculously efficient this season. He completed 23 of 27 passes for 338 yards and three touchdowns in Miami's 52-3 win over Central Michigan, pushing his season completion percentage to an absurd 88.7% . Miami needs to let Mensah attack Clemson early and take the crowd out of the game. Malachi Toney gives him an elite weapon on the outside, while the Hurricanes have enough balance on the ground to prevent Clemson from simply sitting back against the pass. Defensively, the formula is simple: make Clemson throw the football. The Tigers are averaging only 156.3 passing yards per game, while Miami enters with the nation's No. 1 rushing defense at just 39.5 yards allowed per game. If Miami shuts down Clemson's rushing attack early, this matchup could become extremely uncomfortable for the Tigers. How Clemson Wins Clemson needs Death Valley to become a factor immediately. The Tigers cannot afford to get into a shootout with Miami. They need long possessions, a strong rushing performance from Gideon Davidson and at least a couple of turnovers from their defense. Davidson is coming off 159 rushing yards and two touchdowns against Cal , and Clemson will likely need another big performance from him to keep Mensah standing on the sideline. If Clemson falls behind by multiple scores and is forced to throw its way back into the game, Miami has a massive advantage. I think Clemson makes this interesting early. It's a Saturday night game in Death Valley, Clemson has won three straight and the Tigers' defense has shown significant improvement since that LSU embarrassment. But Miami is simply playing at a different level right now. Mensah eventually starts finding holes in the Clemson defense, Miami takes away the Tigers' running game and the Hurricanes begin pulling away in the second half. Clemson has improved, but Miami looks like a legitimate College Football Playoff and national championship contender. This is one heck of a spotlight for just his third start. The Tigers have done their best to alleviate pressure on him with their run game, but Miami leads the ACC with 39.5 rushing yards allowed per game. Clemson may give Gideon Davidson carry after carry, but there will be a time when the Tigers need some big passing plays. Reynolds doesn't have to be Superman, but he has to show some growth. Can he? The combination of a still-developing freshman and an offensive line that's been so-so in pass protection plays into Miami's hands, especially with how much pressure the Hurricanes have been getting on quarterbacks. Clemson is still figuring things out with Reynolds, while Miami has a quarterback with no questions. Darian Mensah will look to do what he did last season at Duke and pick Clemson apart. The Tigers have a strong secondary, but it'll be their toughest challenge yet. Even if Mensah has an off day, the Hurricanes have a strong rushing attack that's gained over 120 yards in all four games. Miami is most likely to have a balanced offense, and it also doesn't have a clear weakness on defense. Clemson's rushing defense struggled against LSU and North Carolina, and while it did better against California, the Golden Bears are averaging an ACC-worst 101.5 rushing yards per game. Ashton Hampton leads the ACC with five pass breakups, and Elliot Washington II is tied for second with three interceptions. Getting Corian Gipson back at nickel would only strengthen an already sound unit. Clemson's secondary will have its hands full though. Mensah has been the nation's most efficient and accurate quarterbacks. But the Tigers are well-equipped to meet the challenge, just like they did against Cal's Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele . Where Miami has an advantage: The Hurricanes look better at the line of scrimmage. Miami ranks second in the ACC with 227.5 rushing yards per game, and running backs Javian Mallory and Mark Fletcher Jr. are averaging 9 and 6.5 yards per carry, respectively. Miami also looks better on the other side. Marquise Lightfoot is tied for fourth in the ACC with four sacks, while Damon Wilson II and Armondo Blount can win one-on-one. Miami generated pressure on 60.8% of Wake Forest's dropbacks in its last ACC game, and Reynolds is 20 of 46 for 175 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions when he's under pressure or blitzed. picks.headline: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire?
picks.blurb: Miami vs. Clemson final score predictions: Will the Hurricanes continue their dominant start, or can the Tigers pull their season out of the fire? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus Division series preview Valkyries take down Wings 49ers owner suspended, fined WNBA playoffs CBS, Tony Romo part ways Sam Navarro-Imagn Images; Ken Ruinard-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 1, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Canes and Tigers will have the eyes of the nation on them on Saturday night in a big game for two programs going in different directions. The Miami Hurricanes and Clemson Tigers square off on Saturday night in Death Valley in a game with significant ACC title implications, with the game being shown in primetime on ABC. The Canes have surged to a 4-0 start, with only a slight flutter in the second half at Wake Forest after leading 31-7 being their only show of mortality thus far. Meanwhile, Clemson has improved to 3-1 after a season-opening 51-10 loss at LSU. Lifeless performances against Georgia Southern and in the first half against UNC have turned into a come from behind win over the Tar Heels and an impressive 24-10 win at Cal last weekend. Can the Tigers ride that modest improvement into an upset win on Saturday night? Our college football writers weighed in with their game predictions. Miami 38, Clemson 28 I think the writing is on the wall for Clemson and Dabo Swinney. The program is a shell of itself, esepcially from a talent acquisition standpoint. Things are the exact opposite for the Hurricanes, as they were less than 70 yards away from a national championship. Even so, I expect Clemson to show out for this game almost as a last ditch effort to save their season. It won't be enough, as the Hurricanes prove to be too explosive for the Tigers. Tyler Forness , A to Z Sports Florida Miami 30, Clemson 10 This game had the potential to be one of the better matchups in the ACC this season if Clemson held up their end of the bargain, but it looks like Dabo and the boys have only fallen further down the list in terms of program competence. The quarterback position is a mess, and a lot of the notable draft prospects heading into the season simply haven't played up to the offseason hype. On the other hand, you have a Miami team with not only one of the sport's most explosive weapons in Malachi Toney, but also one of the most efficient passers in college football in Darian Mensah. I know Clemson is at home, but this has a chance to be a route for the Hurricanes. Give me Miami, big. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Miami 34, Clemson 21 This game is much closer than the final score suggests, with Clemson hanging around for a large portion of the afternoon. One of the biggest storylines will be how the Tigers handle Malachi Toney. It'll be interesting to see if Clemson allows CB Ashton Hampton to follow Toney around the field and essentially shadow him, considering Hampton is the most talented defensive back Miami has faced to this point. If Clemson can limit Toney and force Miami to win elsewhere, the Tigers have a chance to make this uncomfortable. Ultimately, though, Miami's overall talent takes over as the game progresses. The Hurricanes make enough explosive plays on offense to create separation, while Clemson capitalizes on a couple of coverage busts from the Miami secondary for some big plays of its own. Miami's depth and playmakers prove to be the difference in the second half, allowing the Hurricanes to pull away and finish with a 34-21 victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Miami 30, Clemson 13 This feels like a game that could be closer than many pundits are giving it credit for, and perhaps those in Las Vegas as well. The 17-point line feels out of place for what Clemson has been over the last decade, but Dabo Swinney's Tigers have looked anything but the part of contenders the last few years. Clemson's secondary is talented, led by Ashton Hampton, who could play himself into first round consideration in April's NFL Draft. I could see the Tigers giving Miami's offense problems and preventing some of the chunk plays that Miami has ripped off all year with the exception of a quarter and a half against Wake Forest. But Clemson freshman QB Tait Reynolds is going to have a rough experience against a Miami team that's starting to get a tad healthier on the defensive side of the ball. DL Ahmad Moten, Sr. and Armondo Blount are off the injury report and appear set to be available on Saturday, along with CB Damari Brown. Starting CB Xavier Lucas could even possibly be in play, but even if not, Ethan O'Connor has been one of the better CBs in the ACC this year and can handle things very capably. Miami slowly puts this one away in the second half with Mark Fletcher, Jr., who is also off the injury report, pounding away in the fourth quarter on a tired defense. The backfield supporting cast suffered a difficult loss of redshirt junior CharMar "Marty" Brown, who is out for the rest of the season with a severe right knee injury, which was sustained against Wake Forest on Sept. 18. He was the primary backup to Fletcher Jr., but an opportunity for more snaps presents itself. For starters, Fletcher Jr. shouldn't return to a heavy workload. As the Hurricanes' go-to running back, the 21-year-old's long-term availability is valuable. Fletcher Jr. proved to turn things up a notch when the lights got brighter in last year's historic run to the National Championship game. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. home.headline: Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson?
home.blurb: News Sports Restaurants Real Estate Opinion Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals HURRICANES Miami injury report: Is Mark Fletcher playing vs Clemson? Dan Rorabaugh USA TODAY NETWORK - Florida Oct. 3, 2026, 9:01 a.m. ET The Miami football team has been battling injuries all season. But there's been good news coming out of Coral Gables leading up to a prime-time ACC test at Clemson . Fletcher, who led the ACC with 1,192 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns in 2025 and leads the Hurricanes with 230 yards this year, sustained an upper-body injury that forced him to miss most of the fourth quarter in a tighter-than-expected victory against Wake. His health became even more important when No. 2 back Marty Brown was ruled out for the rest of the season after a knee injury earlier in the game. With Moten already out, Miami's other starting defensive tackle, Armondo Blount, got banged up vs. CMU. It was the latest in a string of injuries affecting the Canes' defense, down its two starting cornerbacks — O.J. Frederique and Xavier Lucas — since Week 1. Key backups Ja'Boree Antoine and Damari Brown have also been out, but despite the injuries, UM still fields the No. 2 defense in the nation by yards, No. 4 in points and No. 1 in rush yards. The following players have been ruled out: WR Joshua Moore (out for season), RB CharMar Brown (out for season), DB Ja'Boree Antoine, DB O.J. Frederique, TE Owen Ruskavich, TE Luka Gilbert (out for season). After sitting out last week's game against Central Michigan, running back Mark Fletcher was not on the injury report ahead of today's game at Clemson, signifying he is likely to play. If he is unavailable, Miami will split carries between Javian Mallory, Girard Pringle Jr. and Jordan Lyle with Chris Wheatley-Humphrey sprinked in. Clemson would lean its defense more on containing Malachi Toney and the passing game. Coach Mario Cristobal said running back Mark Fletcher and defensive tackle Ahmad Moten were held out against Central Michigan for precautionary reasons and that both were "ready to roll." Asked about the slew of defenders who missed or were injured during the CMU game, Cristobal said Sept. 28 that the biggest playmakers — Moten and fellow defensive tackle Armondo Blount — were good to go against Clemson. He also said cornerback Xavier Lucas, who was injured in the opener at Stanford and hasn't played since, could be back tonight. Lucas was listed as questionable as of Thursday night. Who benefits if Mark Fletcher is out vs Clemson? Top running back Mark Fletcher Jr. and run-stuffing defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. were among those hurt Sept. 18 at Wake Forest. And while coach Mario Cristobal said the prognosis for both was positive in the week leading up to last week's home date with Central Michigan, both key players were on the sidelines without pads during the 52-3 win . home.blurb: Where No. 4 UM Stands on the ACC’s Initial Injury Report Against Clemson MiamiRoundtable 392 Members • 1,538 Posts MiamiRoundtable MiamiRoundtable Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Where No. 4 UM Stands on the ACC’s Initial Injury Report Against Clemson Anthony Aguirre Partner Oct 1, 2026 12:30 PM Published Oct 1, 2026 12:30 PM The No. 4 Miami Hurricanes secondary attrition and key offensive absences while awaiting game-time decisions on vital defensive depth before a high-stakes, prime-time road test against Clemson. As expected, sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert (undisclosed), redshirt junior running back CharMar “Marty” Brown (right knee), and sophomore wide receiver Joshua Moore (right shoulder) have been ruled out – the case for the rest of the season. Cornerbacks junior Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (left shoulder) and Ja’Boree Antoine (undisclosed) are ruled out for the weekend. Both defenders are expected to return at a later portion of the regular season. Antoine has yet to play and Frederique Jr. has been sidelined since the first drive against Stanford. Newly added to the list, redshirt junior tight end Owen Ruskavich (undisclosed) has been ruled out. He’s logged a new collegiate career high, playing 26 snaps this season. Ruskavich didn’t appear in last Saturday’s 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium. Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. Head coach Mario Cristobal described a return this weekend as “possibly.” Lucas will likely be a game-time decision. The Hurricanes’ secondary has run thin over the last three weeks; a return would add much-needed depth. Sophomore linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. He has shown promising signs this season. Marcelin Jr. is one of nine Hurricanes defenders with at least 10 tackles, including three solos and seven assists, a tackle for loss, and a forced pressure. Clemson has starting junior left guard Elyjah Thurmon (undisclosed) as questionable. Meanwhile, junior nickelback Corian Gipson and fifth-year defensive tackle Devarrick Woods, who missed last Friday’s 24-10 win over Cal, aren’t listed. home.headline: What first Miami-Clemson availability report reveals about key Hurricanes injuries
home.blurb: Junior Xavier Lucas , who hasn't played since the season opener against Stanford , is listed as questionable for Saturday, according to the Atlantic Coast Conference's first availability report for the game released on Wednesday. Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out. As for Clemson, two players are listed as questionable (defensive end Armon Mason and Elyjah Thurmon), while seven have been ruled out (safety Polo Anderson, cornerback Shavar Young Jr., wide receiver Cole Turner , running back David Eziomume, defensive tackles Kourtney Kelly and Markus Strong, and offensive lineman Mason Wade). Hurricanes coach Mario Cristobal on Monday said Lucas was "getting closer" to returning to game action. "Not all the way there yet," Cristobal said. "Hopefully, good news later this week. There's been a lot of progress. Works his butt off, but not all the way there." In their absence, the trio of Ethan O'Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami's primary outside cornerbacks. Speaking of Brown, he did not play last week against Central Michigan but does not have an injury designation, signaling that he should be good to go against Clemson.
